at falde.explanation: "At falde" means "to fall", for example to fall down, or for rain and snow to fall: Jeg faldt af cyklen (I fell off the bike).

sentence.da: Der kan **falde** meget sne i nat.
sentence.en: A lot of snow can fall tonight.

at falde for.explanation: "At falde for" means "to fall for", to suddenly like someone or something a lot: Jeg faldt for ham med det samme (I fell for him right away).

sentence.da: Alle vil **falde for** hendes smil.
sentence.en: Everyone will fall for her smile.

at falde i god jord.explanation: "At falde i god jord" means "to go down well", to be well received. Literally it is to fall in good soil, like a seed that will grow. It is said about ideas, jokes and proposals: Vittigheden faldt i god jord (The joke went down well).

forms.da: det er faldet i god jord

sentence.da: Forslaget kan **falde i god jord** hos ledelsen.
sentence.en: The proposal may go down well with the management.

at falde i søvn.explanation: "At falde i søvn" means "to fall asleep", the moment you drift off: Hun faldt i søvn i toget (She fell asleep on the train). Being asleep is at sove (to sleep): Hun sover (She is sleeping).

sentence.da: Jeg er meget træt og vil snart **falde i søvn**.
sentence.en: I am very tired and will soon fall asleep.

at falde med næsen i smøret.explanation: "At falde med næsen i smøret" means "to strike lucky", to get something good unexpectedly, without much effort. Literally it is to fall with your nose in the butter, a soft landing in something rich.

forms.da: Han faldt med næsen i smøret.
Hun faldt med næsen i smøret med det job.
forms.en: She struck lucky with that job.

forms.da: Vi faldt med næsen i smøret.

sentence.da: Man kan **falde med næsen i smøret**, når man arver et helt hus.
sentence.en: You can strike lucky when you inherit a whole house.

at falde ned.explanation: "At falde ned" means "to fall down", often from a height: Barnet faldt ned fra træet (The child fell down from the tree). For a fall on the ground, plain at falde (to fall) is common: Han faldt på isen (He fell on the ice).

sentence.da: Pas på, du kan **falde ned**!
sentence.en: Be careful, you can fall down!

at falde over.explanation: "At falde over" means "to trip over" something: Jeg faldt over en sten (I tripped over a stone). It can also mean "to come across" something by chance: Jeg faldt over en gammel bog (I came across an old book).

forms.en: I have tripped over / come across

sentence.da: Jeg er bange for at **falde over** hunden.
sentence.en: I am afraid of tripping over the dog.

at falde til ro.explanation: "At falde til ro" means "to calm down", to become quiet after being upset or excited. It is used for something that settles by itself: Barnet faldt til ro (The child calmed down). To calm someone else, use at berolige (to soothe).

sentence.da: Hunden kan ikke **falde til ro**, når der er fest.
sentence.en: The dog cannot calm down when there is a party.

at fange.explanation: "At fange" means "to catch" something moving or someone running away: Politiet fanger tyven (The police catch the thief). For a bus or a train, say at nå (to make it): Jeg når toget (I catch the train).

sentence.da: Kan du **fange** bolden, når jeg kaster?
sentence.en: Can you catch the ball when I throw?

at fare.explanation: "At fare" means "to rush", to move fast, often without stopping. The past form for looks like the small word for (for, as in "for you"), but the rest of the sentence shows which one it is: Bilen for forbi (The car shot past). At fare vild (to get lost) is a common phrase.

sentence.da: Børnene kan **fare** rundt i haven i timevis.
sentence.en: The children can rush around in the garden for hours.

at fare vild.explanation: "At fare vild" means "to get lost", when you do not know where you are: Vi for vild i skoven (We got lost in the forest). To say you lost a thing, use at miste (to lose): Jeg mistede min nøgle (I lost my key).

sentence.da: Uden kort kan vi nemt **fare vild**.
sentence.en: Without a map, we can easily get lost.

at farve.explanation: "At farve" means "to color" or "to dye": Hun farver håret rødt (She dyes her hair red). It also fits coloring in a picture: Børnene farver tegningen (The kids color the drawing).

sentence.da: Hun vil gerne **farve** sit hår rødt.
sentence.en: She would like to dye her hair red.

at faste.explanation: "At faste" means "to fast", to go without food for a period, often for religious reasons or for health: Mange muslimer faster i Ramadanen (Many Muslims fast during Ramadan).

sentence.da: Mange vælger at **faste** i en dag og kun drikke vand.
sentence.en: Many choose to fast for a day and only drink water.

at fastholde.explanation: "At fastholde" means "to maintain" or "to hold on to", to keep something firmly the same even when others disagree: at fastholde sin mening (to stick to your opinion). It can also mean to hold someone firmly in place: at fastholde en mistænkt (to hold a suspect).

forms.en: I have maintained / held on to

sentence.da: Hun vil **fastholde** sin pris, selvom kunden klager.
sentence.en: She wants to maintain her price even though the customer complains.

at fastslå.explanation: "At fastslå" means "to establish" or "to determine", to find out for sure and then state it as a fact: Politiet har fastslået, hvad der skete (The police have established what happened). It is typical for reports, courts and experts.

sentence.da: Eksperterne kan **fastslå**, hvor gammel bygningen er.
sentence.en: The experts can determine how old the building is.

at fastsætte.explanation: "At fastsætte" means "to set" or "to fix", to choose a firm amount, date or rule: at fastsætte en dato (to set a date). Do not mix it up with at fastslå (to establish a fact): you set a date, but you establish what is already true.

sentence.da: Kommunen skal **fastsætte** en pris for parkering.
sentence.en: The municipality must set a price for parking.

at fatte.explanation: "At fatte" means "to grasp" or "to understand". In everyday talk it is the short, casual way to say you get it: Fatter du det? (Do you get it?) With a decision it means to make one: Vi fatter en beslutning (We make a decision).

sentence.da: Reglerne er så svære, at ingen kan **fatte** dem.
sentence.en: The rules are so difficult that no one can understand them.

at feje.explanation: "At feje" means "to sweep", usually with a broom: Jeg fejer gulvet (I sweep the floor). It is for dry dirt like crumbs. Wet cleaning is a different job: Jeg vasker gulvet (I wash the floor).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **feje** køkkenet i dag.
sentence.en: I have to sweep the kitchen today.

at feje noget ind under gulvtæppet.explanation: "At feje noget ind under gulvtæppet" means "to sweep something under the rug", to hide a problem instead of dealing with it. It is the same picture as in English, a mess pushed under the carpet where no one sees it. In use, noget (something) is replaced by the thing itself: at feje problemet ind under gulvtæppet.

forms.en: to sweep the problem under the rug

forms.da: Politikeren fejede sagen ind under gulvtæppet.
forms.en: The politician swept the case under the rug.

forms.da: Vi kan ikke feje det ind under gulvtæppet.
forms.en: We cannot sweep it under the rug.

sentence.da: Firmaet prøvede at **feje noget ind under gulvtæppet**, men det kom frem.
sentence.en: The company tried to sweep something under the rug, but it came out.

at fejle.explanation: "At fejle" means "to fail", and also "to be wrong with": Planen fejlede (The plan failed). Hvad fejler du? (What is wrong with you?) For failing an exam, Danes say at dumpe (to flunk).

sentence.da: Denne plan kan ikke **fejle**.
sentence.en: This plan cannot fail.

at fejre.explanation: "At fejre" means "to celebrate" a day or an event: Vi fejrer jul sammen (We celebrate Christmas together).

sentence.da: Vi vil **fejre** min fødselsdag i weekenden.
sentence.en: We want to celebrate my birthday on the weekend.

at feste.explanation: "At feste" means "to party", meaning to go out and celebrate: Vi fester hele natten (We party all night). A party itself is en fest (a party).

sentence.da: Vi vil **feste** hele natten i weekenden.
sentence.en: We want to party all night this weekend.

at fikse.explanation: "At fikse" means "to fix", to repair something or sort out a problem. It is a relaxed everyday word: Jeg skal nok fikse det (I will sort it out), where a stiffer word like at reparere (to repair) would sound too serious.

sentence.da: Min bror kan **fikse** den gamle cykel på en time.
sentence.en: My brother can fix the old bike in an hour.

at filme.explanation: "At filme" means "to film": Jeg filmer koncerten (I film the concert). A movie is en film: Vi ser en film (We watch a movie).

sentence.da: Må jeg **filme** dig med min telefon?
sentence.en: May I film you with my phone?

at finansiere.explanation: "At finansiere" means "to finance", to provide the money for something big, such as a house, a study or a project. The money can come from savings, a loan or someone else.

sentence.da: Banken vil **finansiere** huset med et lån på tyve år.
sentence.en: The bank will finance the house with a twenty-year loan.

at finde.explanation: "At finde" means "to find", whether you look for something or come across it: Jeg finder mine nøgler (I find my keys). It is also used for opinions: Jeg finder det svært (I find it difficult).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **finde** mine nøgler.
sentence.en: I can't find my keys.

at finde på.explanation: "At finde på" means "to come up with", for ideas and made-up things: Vi fandt på en leg (We came up with a game). Plain at finde means "to find": Jeg finder nøglen (I find the key).

sentence.da: Vi skal **finde på** noget sjovt i weekenden.
sentence.en: We have to come up with something fun this weekend.

at finde ud af.explanation: "At finde ud af" means "to find out" and "to figure out": Jeg finder ud af, hvornår toget kører (I find out when the train leaves). Do not mix it up with at finde på (to come up with).

forms.en: I have found out / figured out

sentence.da: Jeg vil **finde ud af**, hvad der er galt.
sentence.en: I want to find out what is wrong.

at finde vej.explanation: "At finde vej" means "to find one's way", to get to the place you are going: Vi finder vej til hotellet (We find our way to the hotel). It is the opposite of at fare vild (to get lost).

sentence.da: Med et kort kan jeg let **finde vej**.
sentence.en: With a map, I can easily find my way.

at fjerne.explanation: "At fjerne" means "to remove": Jeg fjerner billedet fra væggen (I remove the picture from the wall). It is built from fjern (far away), and the same fjern is in en fjernbetjening (a remote control).

sentence.da: Kan du **fjerne** skoene fra bordet?
sentence.en: Can you take the shoes off the table?

at flirte.explanation: "At flirte" means "to flirt", to show playful romantic interest through looks and jokes. The person you flirt with comes after med (with): Hun flirter med bartenderen (She flirts with the bartender).

sentence.da: Han plejer at **flirte** med alle på kontoret.
sentence.en: He usually flirts with everyone at the office.

at flyde.explanation: "At flyde" means both "to float" and "to flow". Liquids flow: Floden flyder ud i havet (The river flows into the sea). Things that stay on top of water float.

sentence.da: Træ kan **flyde** på vand, men sten kan ikke.
sentence.en: Wood can float on water, but stone cannot.

at flygte.explanation: "At flygte" means "to flee", to get away from danger: Familien flygtede fra krigen (The family fled the war).

sentence.da: De måtte **flygte** fra deres hjem.
sentence.en: They had to flee from their home.

at flytte.explanation: "At flytte" means "to move", either to a new home or to shift something from one place to another: Vi flytter til Aarhus (We are moving to Aarhus). Kan du flytte bilen? (Can you move the car?)

sentence.da: Vi skal **flytte** til et nyt hus.
sentence.en: We are going to move to a new house.

at flytte ind.explanation: "At flytte ind" means "to move in", to start living in a new home: Vi flytter ind på lørdag (We move in on Saturday). Without ind, at flytte means to move something: Jeg flytter bordet (I move the table).

sentence.da: Vi skal **flytte ind** i vores nye hus.
sentence.en: We are going to move into our new house.

at flytte sammen.explanation: "At flytte sammen" means "to move in together": Vi flyttede sammen i maj (We moved in together in May). Sammen (together) is what makes it about sharing a home.

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **flytte sammen** næste år.
sentence.en: We would like to move in together next year.

at flytte sig.explanation: "At flytte sig" means "to move (oneself)", like stepping aside: Kan du flytte dig? (Can you move?) Without sig, at flytte means "to move house" or "to move a thing": Vi flytter til Aarhus (We are moving to Aarhus).

sentence.da: Bilen står i vejen, og han vil ikke **flytte sig**.
sentence.en: The car is in the way, and he won't move.

at flytte ud.explanation: "At flytte ud" means "to move out", to leave a home for good: Min søn flytter ud i august (My son moves out in August). The opposite is at flytte ind (to move in).

sentence.da: Min datter skal **flytte ud** og bo alene.
sentence.en: My daughter is going to move out and live alone.

at flyve.explanation: "At flyve" means "to fly", for birds and for people traveling by plane: Vi flyver til Spanien (We are flying to Spain).

sentence.da: Fuglen kan **flyve** højt.
sentence.en: The bird can fly high.

at flå.explanation: "At flå" means "to rip" or "to skin". It is used for tearing something off or open with force, and for taking the skin off an animal: Han flåede pakken op (He ripped the package open). It is also used for charging far too much: Hotellet flår turisterne (The hotel rips off the tourists).

sentence.da: Slagteren skal **flå** dyret og bruge kødet.
sentence.en: The butcher must skin the animal and use the meat.

at flække.explanation: "At flække" means "to split", to cut or break something into two parts along its length, such as a log.

sentence.da: Man kan **flække** et træstykke med en økse.
sentence.en: You can split a piece of wood with an axe.

at fnise.explanation: "At fnise" means "to giggle", a short, quiet, silly sound of amusement. It often comes when you are nervous or shy: Børnene fnisede bag bogen (The children giggled behind the book).

sentence.da: Eleverne kan ikke lade være med at **fnise** i timen.
sentence.en: The students cannot help giggling in class.

at fodre.explanation: "At fodre" means "to feed", giving food to someone else, like an animal or a baby: Jeg fodrer hunden (I feed the dog). It is not used for feeding yourself.

sentence.da: Jeg skal **fodre** hundene klokken seks.
sentence.en: I have to feed the dogs at six o'clock.

at fokusere.explanation: "At fokusere" means "to focus", to put your attention on one thing. The thing you focus on comes after på (on): Jeg fokuserer på arbejdet (I focus on the work).

sentence.da: Det er svært at **fokusere**, når der er så meget larm.
sentence.en: It is hard to focus when there is so much noise.

at folde.explanation: "At folde" means "to fold", for clothes, paper and towels: Hun folder papiret to gange (She folds the paper twice).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **folde** tøjet og lægge det i skabet.
sentence.en: I have to fold the clothes and put them in the closet.

at forandre.explanation: "At forandre" means "to change", making something different: Du har forandret dig (You have changed). To replace one thing with another, use at skifte (to switch): Jeg skifter job (I am changing jobs).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **forandre** mit liv i år.
sentence.en: I want to change my life this year.

at forandre sig.explanation: "At forandre sig" means "to change", when someone or something becomes different: Byen har forandret sig (The city has changed). Without sig, it means "to change something": Han forandrer planen (He changes the plan).

sentence.da: Mange ting vil **forandre sig** i fremtiden.
sentence.en: Many things will change in the future.

at forankre.explanation: "At forankre" means "to anchor", to fix something firmly in place. It is used for a ship, and for an idea or decision that is rooted in something: Beslutningen er forankret i ledelsen (The decision is anchored in the management).

sentence.da: Vi vil **forankre** den nye plan i hele organisationen.
sentence.en: We want to anchor the new plan across the whole organization.

at forbedre.explanation: "At forbedre" means "to improve", making something better: Vi forbedrer servicen (We are improving the service). It says what you do to something. For something getting better on its own, say at blive bedre (to get better).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **forbedre** mit danske ordforråd.
sentence.en: I would like to improve my Danish vocabulary.

at forbeholde.explanation: "At forbeholde" means "to reserve", to keep something for certain people, not for everyone: Pladsen er forbeholdt gæster (The seat is reserved for guests). With sig (yourself) it is used in the phrase at forbeholde sig retten til (to reserve the right to).

sentence.da: Kommunen vil **forbeholde** den nye parkeringsplads til beboerne.
sentence.en: The municipality will reserve the new parking lot for the residents.

at forberede.explanation: "At forberede" means "to prepare": Hun forbereder middagen (She is preparing dinner). Add sig for yourself: Jeg forbereder mig til prøven (I am getting ready for the test).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **forberede** et møde i morgen.
sentence.en: I have to prepare a meeting tomorrow.

at forberede sig.explanation: "At forberede sig" means "to prepare", getting yourself ready: Jeg forbereder mig til eksamen (I prepare for the exam). Without sig, it means "to prepare something": Hun forbereder et møde (She prepares a meeting).

sentence.da: Eleverne skal **forberede sig** til prøven.
sentence.en: The students have to prepare for the test.

at forbinde.explanation: "At forbinde" means "to connect", and the second thing comes after med (with): Jeg forbinder printeren med computeren (I connect the printer to the computer). It also means "to associate": Jeg forbinder sommer med is (I associate summer with ice cream).

sentence.da: Du kan **forbinde** din telefon med højttaleren.
sentence.en: You can connect your phone to the speaker.

at forblive.explanation: "At forblive" means "to remain", to stay the same and not change: Vi forbliver venner (We remain friends). Compare at blive (to become), which means to change: Hun bliver direktør (She becomes director).

sentence.da: Hun vil **forblive** direktør, selvom firmaet bliver solgt.
sentence.en: She will remain director even though the company is sold.

at forbruge.explanation: "At forbruge" means "to consume", to get through a supply of something, such as water, fuel or money. For a meal, say at spise (to eat); forbruge is for supplies and money.

sentence.da: Vi må **forbruge** mindre strøm, når prisen stiger.
sentence.en: We must consume less electricity when the price rises.

at forbyde.explanation: "At forbyde" means "to forbid" and "to ban": Regeringen forbyder plastikposer (The government bans plastic bags). For a sign, Det er forbudt at ryge her means "Smoking is forbidden here".

sentence.da: Skolen vil **forbyde** mobiler i timerne.
sentence.en: The school wants to ban phones in class.

at fordele.explanation: "At fordele" means "to distribute", to divide something between several people or places so that each gets a part: at fordele arbejdet (to distribute the work). Use mellem (between) before the receivers: Vi fordeler pengene mellem børnene (We distribute the money between the children).

sentence.da: Læreren vil **fordele** eleverne i tre grupper.
sentence.en: The teacher wants to divide the students into three groups.

at fordoble.explanation: "At fordoble" means "to double", to make something twice as big. When it happens by itself, add sig (itself): Antallet fordobler sig hvert år (The number doubles every year).

sentence.da: Firmaet vil **fordoble** produktionen i løbet af to år.
sentence.en: The company wants to double production within two years.

at fordybe sig.explanation: "At fordybe sig" means "to immerse oneself", to give all your attention to one thing for a long time. It is followed by i (in): Han fordyber sig i sin forskning (He immerses himself in his research).

sentence.da: Hun kan **fordybe sig** i en bog i flere timer.
sentence.en: She can immerse herself in a book for hours.

at foregive.explanation: "At foregive" means "to pretend", to claim something that is not true: Han foregav at være syg (He pretended to be sick). In everyday talk, Danes usually say at lade som om (to act as if).

sentence.da: Han kan ikke **foregive**, at han ikke ved noget.
sentence.en: He cannot pretend that he knows nothing.

at foregå.explanation: "At foregå" means "to take place", said about a meeting, a party or a process that is going on somewhere: Mødet foregår i konferencelokalet (The meeting takes place in the conference room). It is for things, never people, so the forms here use det (it).

sentence.da: Hvor skal festen **foregå**?
sentence.en: Where will the party take place?

at forene.explanation: "At forene" means "to unite", to bring separate things or people together into one: at forene to lande (to unite two countries). It also means to combine two things in life: at forene arbejde og familie (to combine work and family).

sentence.da: Musikken kan **forene** mennesker fra hele verden.
sentence.en: Music can unite people from all over the world.

at forenkle.explanation: "At forenkle" means "to simplify", to make something easier and less complicated: at forenkle reglerne (to simplify the rules). It comes from enkel (simple), so it literally means to make something simple.

sentence.da: Vi bør **forenkle** formularen, fordi den er for svær.
sentence.en: We should simplify the form because it is too hard.

at foreslå.explanation: "At foreslå" means "to suggest", putting an idea forward for others to accept or turn down. The idea can follow at (that) or come straight after: Jeg foreslår en anden dag (I suggest another day).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **foreslå**, at vi spiser ude.
sentence.en: I want to suggest that we eat out.

at forestille sig.explanation: "At forestille sig" means "to imagine": Jeg kan ikke forestille mig det (I cannot imagine that). Sig changes with who imagines: mig for jeg (I), dig for du (you).

sentence.da: Hun kan ikke **forestille sig** livet uden musik.
sentence.en: She cannot imagine life without music.

at forestå.explanation: "At forestå" means "to be in charge of", to run something and take responsibility for it: Hun forestår afdelingen (She is in charge of the department). It also means "to lie ahead" about what is coming: Der forestår en svær tid (A hard time lies ahead).

forms.en: to be in charge of / lie ahead
I have been in charge of

sentence.da: En erfaren leder skal **forestå** projektet og holde styr på pengene.
sentence.en: An experienced leader must be in charge of the project and keep track of the money.

at foretage.explanation: "At foretage" means "to carry out", used before something you do on purpose: at foretage en ændring (to make a change), at foretage et opkald (to make a call). For making objects like a cake, say at lave (to make) instead.

sentence.da: Lægen skal **foretage** en lille undersøgelse i morgen.
sentence.en: The doctor will carry out a small examination tomorrow.

at foretrække.explanation: "At foretrække" means "to prefer": Hun foretrækker at gå (She prefers to walk). To say what you like less, add frem for (over): Jeg foretrækker hunde frem for katte (I prefer dogs to cats).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **foretrække** te frem for kaffe.
sentence.en: I would prefer tea to coffee.

at forfalde.explanation: "At forfalde" means "to fall due" and "to decay". A payment falls due on a set day: Fakturaen forfalder om fjorten dage (The invoice falls due in fourteen days). A building or a person can also decay.

sentence.da: Uden vedligehold vil huset hurtigt **forfalde**.
sentence.en: Without upkeep the house will quickly decay.

at forfatte.explanation: "At forfatte" means "to author", to put together a text with care, such as a speech or an official document: Hun forfattede et brev til ministeren (She drew up a letter to the minister).

sentence.da: Borgmesteren vil **forfatte** en tale til festen.
sentence.en: The mayor will compose a speech for the party.

at forfremme.explanation: "At forfremme" means "to promote", but only in the sense of moving a person up to a better job. To promote a product, Danes say at markedsføre (to market).

sentence.da: Chefen vil **forfremme** hende, fordi hun arbejder så hårdt.
sentence.en: The boss wants to promote her because she works so hard.

at forfølge.explanation: "At forfølge" means "to pursue", to follow someone closely in order to reach them, or to follow a goal: at forfølge sin drøm (to pursue your dream). It also means "to persecute", to treat a group of people cruelly because of who they are.

sentence.da: Politiet kan ikke **forfølge** bilen længere, fordi den er for hurtig.
sentence.en: The police cannot pursue the car any longer because it is too fast.

at forføre.explanation: "At forføre" means "to seduce": to win someone over romantically. It can also mean to lead someone into something they should not do, so the word is not only about love.

sentence.da: Skurken vil **forføre** hende og få hendes penge.
sentence.en: The villain wants to seduce her and get her money.

at forhandle.explanation: "At forhandle" means "to negotiate", for example prices, contracts or pay. You negotiate about something with om (about): forhandle om prisen (negotiate the price). Be careful: en forhandler is not a negotiator but a dealer or retailer, such as a car dealer.

sentence.da: Vi vil **forhandle** om prisen.
sentence.en: We want to negotiate the price.

at forhindre.explanation: "At forhindre" means "to prevent", stopping something from happening: Vaccinen forhindrer sygdom (The vaccine prevents illness). With a person, add i at (from) before the action: Regnen forhindrede os i at gå (The rain stopped us from going).

sentence.da: Vi kan **forhindre** mange ulykker med bedre veje.
sentence.en: We can prevent many accidents with better roads.

at forhøre sig.explanation: "At forhøre sig" means "to inquire", to check something with a person or an office before you decide. The thing you check on comes after om (about): Jeg forhører mig om åbningstiderne (I am checking on the opening hours). Without sig (oneself), at forhøre means to interrogate, which is what police do.

sentence.da: Han vil **forhøre sig** om prisen i butikken.
sentence.en: He wants to inquire about the price at the shop.

at forklare.explanation: "At forklare" means "to explain". Danish says forklare noget for nogen (explain something to someone): Kan du forklare det for mig? (Can you explain it to me?).

sentence.da: Læreren vil **forklare** ordet.
sentence.en: The teacher will explain the word.

at forklæde sig.explanation: "At forklæde sig" means "to disguise oneself": to dress so that people do not recognize you. Add som to say as what: Hun forklædte sig som tjener (She disguised herself as a waiter).

sentence.da: Tyven vil **forklæde sig** som politibetjent og gå ind i banken.
sentence.en: The thief wants to disguise himself as a police officer and go into the bank.

at forkorte.explanation: "At forkorte" means "to shorten", to make something shorter in time or length: at forkorte talen (to shorten the speech). With a word it means to abbreviate it, and the result is called en forkortelse (an abbreviation).

sentence.da: Vi kan **forkorte** turen ved at tage motorvejen.
sentence.en: We can shorten the trip by taking the highway.

at forkæle.explanation: "At forkæle" means "to spoil" in the kind sense, to pamper: to treat someone to nice things: Jeg vil forkæle dig i dag (I want to pamper you today). With children it can also be negative, when they get too much and expect it.

sentence.da: Bedsteforældrene vil **forkæle** børnebørnene med is og slik.
sentence.en: The grandparents want to spoil the grandchildren with ice cream and candy.

at forlade.explanation: "At forlade" means "to leave" a place or a person: Hun forlod huset kl. 8 (She left the house at 8). Hun forlod ham (She left him). For simply going away, use at gå (to go): Jeg går nu (I am leaving now).

sentence.da: Han vil **forlade** landet i næste måned.
sentence.en: He will leave the country next month.

at forlange.explanation: "At forlange" means "to demand", to ask for something firmly because you think you have a right to it: Han forlangte sine penge tilbage (He demanded his money back). It is stronger than politely asking.

sentence.da: Du kan **forlange** en ny vare, hvis den er gået i stykker.
sentence.en: You can demand a new item if it has broken.

at forlove sig.explanation: "At forlove sig" means "to get engaged", the promise to marry someone before the wedding. The person you get engaged to comes after med (with): Hun forlovede sig med Peter i sommer (She got engaged to Peter last summer).

sentence.da: Han har en ring og vil **forlove sig** med hende.
sentence.en: He has a ring and wants to get engaged to her.

at forlænge.explanation: "At forlænge" means "to extend", to make something longer, in time or in size: at forlænge et visum (to extend a visa), at forlænge et bord (to make a table longer).

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **forlænge** vores ophold med to dage.
sentence.en: We would like to extend our stay by two days.

at forløbe.explanation: "At forløbe" means "to proceed" or "to go", and tells how an event develops from start to finish. It is used for events and processes, not for people: Festen forløb roligt (The party went calmly).

forms.en: it has proceeded / gone (well or badly)

sentence.da: En operation som denne kan **forløbe** uden problemer.
sentence.en: An operation like this can go without problems.

at formidle.explanation: "At formidle" means "to convey" or "to mediate": to get something across between people, such as knowledge, news or a deal: Læreren formidler viden til eleverne (The teacher conveys knowledge to the students).

sentence.da: En god journalist kan **formidle** svære ting på en enkel måde.
sentence.en: A good journalist can convey difficult things in a simple way.

at formindske.explanation: "At formindske" means "to reduce", to make something smaller in size, amount or effect: at formindske udgifterne (to reduce the costs). Danes also say at mindske, which means the same.

sentence.da: Mere motion kan **formindske** risikoen for sygdom.
sentence.en: More exercise can reduce the risk of illness.

at formode.explanation: "At formode" means "to suppose" or "to presume": to take something as true on good grounds without being sure. It rests on reasons, so it is more than a hunch.

sentence.da: Vi kan **formode**, at toget er forsinket på grund af sneen.
sentence.en: We can presume that the train is late because of the snow.

at formulere.explanation: "At formulere" means "to formulate", to put a thought into clear words in speech or writing: at formulere et spørgsmål (to put a question into words).

sentence.da: Det er svært at **formulere** sine tanker på et fremmedsprog.
sentence.en: It is hard to put your thoughts into words in a foreign language.

at fornemme.explanation: "At fornemme" means "to sense", to notice something you cannot see or prove, like a mood or a danger: Jeg fornemmer, at der er noget galt (I sense that something is wrong).

sentence.da: Hunden kan **fornemme**, når ejeren er ked af det.
sentence.en: The dog can sense when its owner is sad.

at forny.explanation: "At forny" means "to renew", to make something fresh again or valid for another period: at forny sit kørekort (to renew your driver's license).

sentence.da: Du skal **forny** dit pas, før du rejser.
sentence.en: You must renew your passport before you travel.

at fornægte.explanation: "At fornægte" means "to deny": to refuse to accept that something is real, such as the truth or your own feelings. For simply denying a charge against you, at nægte (to deny / refuse) is more usual.

sentence.da: Du kan ikke **fornægte** din fortid.
sentence.en: You cannot deny your past.

at fornærme.explanation: "At fornærme" means "to offend", to hurt someone's feelings or pride with what you say or do: Undskyld, hvis jeg fornærmede dig (Sorry if I offended you).

sentence.da: Du kan **fornærme** folk, hvis du er for direkte.
sentence.en: You can offend people if you are too direct.

at forpligte.explanation: "At forpligte" means "to commit" or "to oblige": to tie someone to doing something through an agreement or a rule. Add sig when you tie yourself: Jeg forpligter mig til at komme (I commit myself to coming).

sentence.da: En underskrift kan **forpligte** dig til at betale.
sentence.en: A signature can commit you to paying.

at forråde.explanation: "At forråde" means "to betray": to break someone's trust, for example by turning on a friend or giving away a secret. It can also be a thing that gives you away: Hans smil forrådte ham (His smile gave him away).

sentence.da: Man må aldrig **forråde** en ven, der stoler på en.
sentence.en: You must never betray a friend who trusts you.

at forsikre.explanation: "At forsikre" means both "to assure" and "to insure". To assure is to tell someone that something is certain: Jeg forsikrer dig om, at det er sikkert (I assure you it is safe). To insure is to buy cover against damage: at forsikre bilen (to insure the car), and the cover itself is en forsikring (an insurance).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **forsikre** huset mod brand og tyveri.
sentence.en: I want to insure the house against fire and theft.

at forsinke.explanation: "At forsinke" means "to delay", making something late: Snevejret forsinker toget (The snowstorm delays the train). The train itself is forsinket (delayed): Toget er forsinket (The train is delayed).

sentence.da: Trafikken kan **forsinke** os med en time.
sentence.en: The traffic can delay us by an hour.

at forske.explanation: "At forske" means "to research", to dig deep into a subject, often at a university, to find new knowledge. The subject comes after i (in): Hun har forsket i kræft i ti år (She has researched cancer for ten years).

sentence.da: Hun vil **forske** i, hvorfor bier forsvinder.
sentence.en: She wants to research why bees are disappearing.

at forskrække.explanation: "At forskrække" means "to frighten", usually a sudden little shock, like someone jumping out at you. A longer fear is closer to at skræmme (to scare).

sentence.da: Et højt knald kan **forskrække** børnene, fordi det kommer pludseligt.
sentence.en: A loud bang can frighten the children because it comes suddenly.

at forskyde.explanation: "At forskyde" means "to shift" or "to displace": to put something a little away from where it was, in place or in time. Forskudt arbejdstid means working hours that start at different times (staggered hours).

sentence.da: Et jordskælv kan **forskyde** jordlagene under byen.
sentence.en: An earthquake can shift the layers of earth under the city.

at forsone sig.explanation: "At forsone sig" means "to reconcile": to end a quarrel and be on good terms again, or to accept something hard. Add med and the person: Jeg vil forsone mig med min bror (I want to reconcile with my brother).

sentence.da: Efter mange års skænderi vil brødrene gerne **forsone sig**.
sentence.en: After many years of quarreling the brothers want to reconcile.

at forstyrre.explanation: "At forstyrre" means "to disturb": Jeg vil ikke forstyrre dig (I do not want to disturb you). To ask politely when you walk in, say Må jeg forstyrre? (May I interrupt?)

sentence.da: Børnene må ikke **forstyrre** hende, når hun arbejder.
sentence.en: The children must not disturb her when she works.

at forstå.explanation: "At forstå" means "to understand": Jeg forstår ikke (I don't understand). To say you know a fact, use at vide (to know) instead: Jeg ved det ikke (I don't know).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **forstå** ham.
sentence.en: I cannot understand him.

at forstærke.explanation: "At forstærke" means "to reinforce", to make something stronger or louder, such as a wall, a feeling or a sound: at forstærke lyden (to amplify the sound). The device that does it is en forstærker (an amplifier).

sentence.da: Vi må **forstærke** broen, før tunge biler kører over den.
sentence.en: We must reinforce the bridge before heavy cars drive over it.

at forsvare.explanation: "At forsvare" means "to defend", to keep someone or something safe when it is under threat, in a war, in sport or in an argument: at forsvare sin mening (to defend your opinion). Denmark's armed forces are called Forsvaret (the Defense).

sentence.da: Soldaterne skal **forsvare** grænsen mod fjenden.
sentence.en: The soldiers must defend the border against the enemy.

at forsvinde.explanation: "At forsvinde" means "to disappear" or "to vanish": Solen forsvandt bag skyerne (The sun disappeared behind the clouds).

sentence.da: Tyven kan **forsvinde** i mængden.
sentence.en: The thief can disappear in the crowd.

at forsyne.explanation: "At forsyne" means "to supply", to provide someone or something with what is needed: at forsyne byen med vand (to supply the city with water). The thing you give comes after med (with). At a meal, Forsyn dig! means "Help yourself!".

sentence.da: Vindmøllerne kan **forsyne** tusind hjem med strøm.
sentence.en: The wind turbines can supply a thousand homes with electricity.

at forsøge.explanation: "At forsøge" means "to attempt" or "to try": Jeg forsøger at forstå (I am trying to understand). Unlike at prøve (to try), it is not used for trying out or tasting: Jeg prøver kagen (I try the cake).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **forsøge** at komme i morgen.
sentence.en: I will try to come tomorrow.

at forsømme.explanation: "At forsømme" means "to neglect", to fail to give something the care or time it needs: at forsømme sin have (to neglect your garden). At school it also means to miss lessons: en elev, der forsømmer undervisningen (a student who skips class).

sentence.da: Man må ikke **forsømme** sine tænder, hvis man vil beholde dem.
sentence.en: You must not neglect your teeth if you want to keep them.

at forsørge.explanation: "At forsørge" means "to support (financially)": to earn the money that others live on, like children or a family. It is not the word for help or encouragement, which is at støtte (to support).

related.en: to feed / provide a living for

sentence.da: Hun skal **forsørge** tre børn og arbejder to steder.
sentence.en: She has to support three children and works in two places.

at fortage sig.explanation: "At fortage sig" means "to wear off": to go away slowly by itself, usually a feeling or a pain, without anyone doing anything: Hans vrede fortog sig (His anger wore off).

sentence.da: Smerten i foden vil **fortage sig** af sig selv.
sentence.en: The pain in the foot will wear off on its own.

at fortie.explanation: "At fortie" means "to conceal": to keep quiet about a fact that others ought to be told, such as a mistake or a risk. It is about what you do not say, not about hiding an object.

forms.en: I have concealed / kept quiet about

sentence.da: Sælgeren må ikke **fortie**, at bilen har skader.
sentence.en: The seller must not conceal that the car has damage.

at fortjene.explanation: "At fortjene" means "to deserve": Du fortjener en pause (You deserve a break). It is built on at tjene (to earn), but earning money uses tjene alone: Jeg tjener penge (I earn money).

sentence.da: Hun har trænet hårdt og kan **fortjene** prisen.
sentence.en: She has trained hard and may deserve the prize.

at fortolke.explanation: "At fortolke" means "to interpret", to work out what a text, a rule, a dream or a signal means. Different people can reach different results: Man kan fortolke et digt på mange måder (A poem can be read in many ways).

sentence.da: Hvert land kan **fortolke** reglerne på sin egen måde.
sentence.en: Each country can interpret the rules in its own way.

at fortryde.explanation: "At fortryde" means "to regret": Jeg fortryder det ikke (I do not regret it). To say what you regret, add at (that): Jeg fortryder, at jeg sagde det (I regret that I said it).

sentence.da: Du kommer til at **fortryde** det senere.
sentence.en: You will regret it later.

at fortrænge.explanation: "At fortrænge" means "to repress": to push a painful memory out of your mind so you do not think about it. It also means "to displace", when something takes the place of something else: Bilen har fortrængt hesten (The car has displaced the horse).

sentence.da: Hjernen kan **fortrænge** minder, der gør for ondt.
sentence.en: The brain can repress memories that hurt too much.

at fortsætte.explanation: "At fortsætte" means "to continue": Vi fortsætter i morgen (We continue tomorrow). To keep doing something, add med at (-ing): Fortsæt med at læse! (Keep reading!)

sentence.da: Efter pausen kan vi **fortsætte** timen.
sentence.en: After the break, we can continue the class.

at fortsætte med.explanation: "At fortsætte med" means "to continue with" something you are already doing: Vi fortsætter med lektionen (We continue with the lesson). To just keep going, say Fortsæt! (Keep going!).

sentence.da: Vi kan **fortsætte med** øvelsen efter pausen.
sentence.en: We can continue with the exercise after the break.

at fortælle.explanation: "At fortælle" means "to tell", especially to tell a story or give someone information: Han fortæller om sin rejse (He tells about his trip). For simply saying a few words, use at sige (to say): Han siger hej (He says hello). You can add who you tell: fortælle nogen noget (tell someone something).

sentence.da: Min mormor vil **fortælle** en historie til børnene.
sentence.en: My grandmother will tell the children a story.

at forudse.explanation: "At forudse" means "to foresee": to see beforehand what is going to happen. You use it for what you can work out or reckon on, such as a price rise: Vi forudser en prisstigning (We foresee a price rise).

sentence.da: Ingen kan **forudse** vejret om en måned.
sentence.en: No one can foresee the weather in a month.

at forudsige.explanation: "At forudsige" means "to predict", to say what will happen before it happens: at forudsige valgresultatet (to predict the election result). It is built from forud (ahead) and sige (to say), so it is literally "to say ahead".

sentence.da: Ingen kan **forudsige**, hvordan vejret bliver i næste måned.
sentence.en: No one can predict what the weather will be next month.

at forurene.explanation: "At forurene" means "to pollute", to make air, water or soil dirty and harmful with waste or chemicals: Fabrikken forurenede floden (The factory polluted the river).

sentence.da: Biler og fabrikker kan **forurene** luften i store byer.
sentence.en: Cars and factories can pollute the air in big cities.

at forvandle.explanation: "At forvandle" means "to transform", to turn something completely into something else: Heksen forvandlede prinsen til en frø (The witch turned the prince into a frog). The new form comes after til (into).

sentence.da: Maling kan **forvandle** et gammelt værelse til et nyt.
sentence.en: Paint can transform an old room into a new one.

at forvente.explanation: "At forvente" means "to expect", when you think something will happen: Jeg forventer et svar snart (I expect an answer soon). It can also mean requiring something of someone: Vi forventer, at du kommer til tiden (We expect you to be on time).

sentence.da: Vi kan **forvente** regn i morgen.
sentence.en: We can expect rain tomorrow.

at forvirre.explanation: "At forvirre" means "to confuse", to make someone unsure or unable to think clearly: Vejskiltene forvirrer mig (The road signs confuse me).

sentence.da: Alle de nye regler kan **forvirre** gæsterne.
sentence.en: All the new rules can confuse the guests.

at forværre.explanation: "At forværre" means "to worsen", making something worse: Regnen forværrer trafikken (The rain makes the traffic worse). It is the opposite of at forbedre (to improve).

sentence.da: Dårlig søvn kan **forværre** smerterne.
sentence.en: Poor sleep can worsen the pain.

at forårsage.explanation: "At forårsage" means "to cause", to make something happen, most often something bad: at forårsage skade (to cause damage). It is a formal word. In everyday speech Danes often say noget fører til (something leads to) instead.

sentence.da: Is på vejene kan **forårsage** mange ulykker om vinteren.
sentence.en: Ice on the roads can cause many accidents in the winter.

at forære.explanation: "At forære" means "to give (as a gift)": to give something freely, with nothing wanted back, often as an honor or a surprise. The person who gets it comes right after the word, with no til: Han forærede hende en ring (He gave her a ring as a gift).

sentence.da: Farfar vil **forære** mig sit gamle ur.
sentence.en: Grandpa wants to give me his old watch as a gift.

at fotografere.explanation: "At fotografere" means "to photograph": Jeg fotograferer huset (I photograph the house). Danes more often say at tage et billede af (to take a picture of): Jeg tager et billede af huset (I take a picture of the house).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **fotografere** solnedgangen med min telefon.
sentence.en: I want to photograph the sunset with my phone.

at fremføre.explanation: "At fremføre" means "to present" or "to put forward": to say a view or an argument out loud so others hear it. It also means to perform a song or a piece of music before an audience: Koret fremførte en salme (The choir performed a hymn).

sentence.da: Eleverne skal **fremføre** et teaterstykke for forældrene.
sentence.en: The students are going to perform a play for the parents.

at fremhæve.explanation: "At fremhæve" means "to emphasize" or "to highlight", to make something stand out so people notice it. It works for text, clothes and speech: at fremhæve en pointe (to stress a point).

sentence.da: Den røde farve kan **fremhæve** dine øjne.
sentence.en: The red color can make your eyes stand out.

at fremkalde.explanation: "At fremkalde" means "to cause": to make a reaction or a feeling appear, like laughter or anger. It also means "to develop" a photo from film: Jeg fremkalder billederne i aften (I am developing the pictures tonight).

sentence.da: Stærk sol kan **fremkalde** hovedpine hos nogle mennesker.
sentence.en: Strong sun can cause headaches in some people.

at fremkomme.explanation: "At fremkomme" means "to emerge" or "to appear": to come into view or become known, often about facts, results and ideas. Fremkomme med is to come up with a claim: Han fremkom med en ny teori (He came up with a new theory).

sentence.da: Nye fakta kan **fremkomme** under retssagen.
sentence.en: New facts can emerge during the trial.

at fremlægge.explanation: "At fremlægge" means "to present": to put a plan, a report or a proposal before others so they can read it or decide. At school, students also use it for giving a talk about their work: Vi skal fremlægge i morgen (We are presenting tomorrow).

sentence.da: Direktøren skal **fremlægge** årsregnskabet på mødet.
sentence.en: The director is going to present the annual accounts at the meeting.

at fremme.explanation: "At fremme" means "to promote" or "to further": to help something develop or succeed. It is used for good things, such as health, trade or understanding: Motion fremmer sundheden (Exercise promotes health).

sentence.da: Kommunen vil **fremme** cykling med flere cykelstier.
sentence.en: The town wants to promote cycling with more bike lanes.

at fremskynde.explanation: "At fremskynde" means "to speed up": to make a process or a decision happen sooner. For a vehicle going faster, use at accelerere (to accelerate).

sentence.da: Flere hænder kan **fremskynde** arbejdet og spare os tid.
sentence.en: More hands can speed up the work and save us time.

at fremstille.explanation: "At fremstille" means "to produce" or "to portray". For things, it is to make them, often in a factory or workshop: at fremstille møbler (to produce furniture). For a person or event, it is to show them in a certain way: Avisen fremstiller ham som en helt (The newspaper portrays him as a hero).

sentence.da: Fabrikken kan **fremstille** tusind cykler om dagen.
sentence.en: The factory can produce a thousand bikes per day.

at fremvise.explanation: "At fremvise" means "to display" or "to show": to hold something up for others to look at or check, such as a ticket, a passport or a collection. In everyday talk, at vise (to show) is the usual word: Vis mig billedet (Show me the picture).

sentence.da: Du skal **fremvise** din billet, når kontrolløren spørger.
sentence.en: You must show your ticket when the inspector asks.

at fri.explanation: "At fri" means "to propose", as in asking someone to marry you. The person you ask comes after til (to): Han friede til hende (He proposed to her).

sentence.da: Han vil **fri** til hende i aften.
sentence.en: He is going to propose to her tonight.

at frifinde.explanation: "At frifinde" means "to acquit": when a court decides that someone is not guilty and may go free. The opposite is at dømme (to convict): Dommeren frifandt ham (The judge acquitted him).

sentence.da: Retten vil **frifinde** ham, fordi der ikke er nogen beviser.
sentence.en: The court will acquit him because there is no evidence.

at frigive.explanation: "At frigive" means "to release", to let go of something that was held back, such as a person, money or secret documents: Politiet frigav manden (The police released the man). For a book or an album, Danes say at udgive (to publish).

sentence.da: Retten vil **frigive** fangen, fordi der ikke er beviser.
sentence.en: The court will release the prisoner because there is no evidence.

at fritage.explanation: "At fritage" means "to exempt": to free someone from a duty, a rule or a payment. Add for to say what from: Han blev fritaget for gymnastik (He was exempted from gym).

sentence.da: Lægen kan **fritage** dig fra arbejde, når du er syg.
sentence.en: The doctor can exempt you from work when you are sick.

at frygte.explanation: "At frygte" means "to fear", which sounds more serious than being scared: De frygter det værste (They fear the worst). For everyday fear, Danes say at være bange for (to be afraid of): Jeg er bange for hunde (I am afraid of dogs).

sentence.da: Vi må ikke **frygte** fremtiden.
sentence.en: We must not fear the future.

at fryse.explanation: "At fryse" means "to freeze" and also "to feel cold": Jeg fryser (I am cold, literally I freeze). It also describes water turning to ice: Vandet fryser (The water freezes). Do not mix it up with en fryser (a freezer).

sentence.da: Uden jakke vil du **fryse**.
sentence.en: Without a jacket you will freeze.

at fuldende.explanation: "At fuldende" means "to complete", to finish something fully, often a big or careful piece of work: at fuldende et maleri (to complete a painting). It is stronger than at afslutte (to end): fuldende means that nothing is missing.

sentence.da: Han vil **fuldende** romanen, før han bliver halvfjerds.
sentence.en: He wants to complete the novel before he turns seventy.

at fuldføre.explanation: "At fuldføre" means "to complete", to take something you started all the way to the end, such as a course or a project.

sentence.da: Han vil **fuldføre** sin uddannelse og blive lærer.
sentence.en: He wants to complete his education and become a teacher.

at fungere.explanation: "At fungere" means "to work", when a thing does what it should: Min telefon fungerer ikke (My phone does not work). For a person at a job, use at arbejde (to work).

sentence.da: Tror du, at planen kan **fungere**?
sentence.en: Do you think the plan can work?

at fylde.explanation: "At fylde" means "to fill": Jeg fylder glasset med vand (I fill the glass with water). It also means "to take up space": Sofaen fylder meget (The sofa takes up a lot of space). For a birthday, it means "to turn": Jeg fylder 30 i dag (I turn 30 today).

forms.en: I have filled / taken up space

sentence.da: Børnene må **fylde** posen med slik.
sentence.en: The children may fill the bag with candy.

at fylde op.explanation: "At fylde op" means "to fill up". Op (up) says you fill it to the top, so it is more complete than plain at fylde (to fill): Jeg fylder kanden op (I fill up the pitcher).

sentence.da: Vi skal **fylde op** med benzin i morgen.
sentence.en: We have to fill up with gas tomorrow.

at fylde år.explanation: "At fylde år" means "to have a birthday", in the sense of turning a certain age. You can add the age: Jeg fylder tredive år (I am turning thirty). At have fødselsdag (to have a birthday) just says it is your birthday, without the age.

sentence.da: Min far skal **fylde år** i morgen.
sentence.en: My dad has a birthday tomorrow.

at fyre.explanation: "At fyre" means "to fire" someone from a job: Chefen fyrede ham (The boss fired him). It also means "to make a fire": Vi fyrer i brændeovnen (We light the wood stove).

sentence.da: Firmaet må **fyre** ti medarbejdere.
sentence.en: The company has to fire ten employees.

at få.explanation: "At få" means "to get" or "to receive": Jeg får et brev (I get a letter). It also appears in få lov (to be allowed): Jeg fik lov (I was allowed). It does not mean to go and fetch something; for that, use at hente (to fetch).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **få** en gave til min fødselsdag.
sentence.en: I am going to get a present for my birthday.

at få besked.explanation: "At få besked" means "to be notified", to hear what is going on: Jeg fik besked om mødet (I was told about the meeting). The person who tells you uses at give besked (to let someone know).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **få besked**, når pakken kommer.
sentence.en: I will be notified when the package arrives.

at få besøg.explanation: "At få besøg" means "to have visitors", when someone comes to see you: Vi får besøg i weekenden (We have visitors this weekend). To go see someone yourself, say at være på besøg (to be visiting): Jeg er på besøg hos min mor (I am visiting my mother).

sentence.da: Jeg rydder op, fordi jeg skal **få besøg**.
sentence.en: I am tidying up because I am having guests.

at få det bedre.explanation: "At få det bedre" means "to feel better" after being sick or sad: Jeg håber, du får det bedre (I hope you feel better). To wish someone well, say God bedring! (Get well soon!)

sentence.da: Med lidt hvile vil du **få det bedre**.
sentence.en: With some rest, you will feel better.

at få et barn.explanation: "At få et barn" means "to have a baby", literally to get a child: Vi får et barn i maj (We are having a baby in May).

sentence.da: Min søster er gravid og skal **få et barn**.
sentence.en: My sister is pregnant and is going to have a baby.

at få fat i.explanation: "At få fat i" means "to get hold of", for grabbing a thing or reaching a person: Jeg fik fat i rebet (I grabbed the rope). Jeg kunne ikke få fat i ham (I could not reach him).

sentence.da: Barnet kan ikke **få fat i** kagen på hylden.
sentence.en: The child cannot get hold of the cake on the shelf.

at få fri.explanation: "At få fri" means "to get off", to be allowed to leave work or school: Vi får fri klokken tre (We get off at three). When you decide to take a day yourself, use at tage fri (to take time off).

forms.en: I have gotten off (work or school)

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **få fri** tidligt i dag.
sentence.en: I would like to get off early today.

at få hjælp.explanation: "At få hjælp" means "to get help": Kan jeg få hjælp? (Can I get help?). Danish says hjælp (help) with no en (a) in front: Jeg har brug for hjælp (I need help).

sentence.da: Jeg er syg og vil **få hjælp**.
sentence.en: I am sick and want to get help.

at få kolde fødder.explanation: "At få kolde fødder" means "to get cold feet": to suddenly feel afraid or unsure just before doing something big, like a wedding or signing a contract. It is only about nerves, not about being cold.

sentence.da: Mange kan **få kolde fødder**, når bryllupsdagen nærmer sig.
sentence.en: Many people can get cold feet when the wedding day gets close.

at få lov til.explanation: "At få lov til" means "to be allowed to", when someone gives you permission: Jeg fik lov til at gå hjem (I was allowed to go home).

sentence.da: Børnene vil gerne **få lov til** at blive længe.
sentence.en: The children would like to be allowed to stay longer.

at få lyst til.explanation: "At få lyst til" means "to feel like", when a wish suddenly appears: Jeg fik lyst til kage (I felt like having cake). Before an action, add at (to): Jeg fik lyst til at gå en tur (I felt like going for a walk).

sentence.da: Når solen skinner, kan man **få lyst til** is.
sentence.en: When the sun shines, you can feel like having ice cream.

at få nok.explanation: "At få nok" means "to have had enough", or "to get fed up": Nu har jeg fået nok! (Now I have had enough!) It can also be about food: Har du fået nok at spise? (Have you had enough to eat?)

forms.en: I get fed up (have had enough)

sentence.da: Jeg begynder at **få nok** af støjen.
sentence.en: I am starting to get fed up with the noise.

at få ondt af.explanation: "At få ondt af" means "to feel sorry for" someone: Jeg får ondt af hende (I feel sorry for her). Do not mix it up with at have ondt i (to hurt in): Jeg har ondt i maven (My stomach hurts).

sentence.da: Man kan ikke andet end **få ondt af** ham.
sentence.en: You cannot help feeling sorry for him.

at få ret.explanation: "At få ret" means "to be proven right": Jeg fik ret (I was proven right). Being right is at have ret: Du har ret (You are right).

sentence.da: Jeg tror, hun vil **få ret** til sidst.
sentence.en: I think she will be proven right in the end.

at få styr på.explanation: "At få styr på" means "to get control of", or "to sort out", something messy: Jeg skal få styr på min økonomi (I must sort out my finances). The result is at have styr på (to have it under control).

forms.en: to get control of / sort out
I get control of / sort out
I got control of / sorted out
I have gotten control of / sorted out

sentence.da: Vi skal **få styr på** rodet i garagen.
sentence.en: We have to sort out the mess in the garage.

at få tid.explanation: "At få tid" means "to find time": Jeg fik tid til at læse (I found time to read). It also means "to get an appointment", for example at the doctor or the hairdresser. To be free right now, use at have tid (to have time).

related.en: to have time to / make it

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **få tid** hos lægen før mandag.
sentence.en: I can't get an appointment with the doctor before Monday.

at få travlt.explanation: "At få travlt" means "to get busy": Vi fik travlt i går (We got busy yesterday). When you are already busy, use at have travlt: Jeg har travlt (I am busy).

sentence.da: Vi vil **få travlt**, når gæsterne kommer.
sentence.en: We will get busy when the guests arrive.

at få øje på.explanation: "At få øje på" means "to catch sight of", the moment you first notice something: Jeg fik øje på en ræv (I spotted a fox). It is about the first glimpse, not just looking.

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **få øje på** bussen endnu.
sentence.en: I can't spot the bus yet.

at føde.explanation: "At føde" means "to give birth", for a woman or an animal having a baby: Hun føder en datter (She gives birth to a daughter). To say you were born, use at blive født (to be born): Jeg blev født i Aarhus (I was born in Aarhus).

sentence.da: Kvinden skal **føde** barnet på hospitalet.
sentence.en: The woman is going to give birth to the baby at the hospital.

at fødes.explanation: "At fødes" means "to be born", but in everyday speech people say at blive født (to become born): Jeg blev født i 1990 (I was born in 1990).

sentence.da: Vores barn skal **fødes** i maj.
sentence.en: Our child is due to be born in May.

at føle.explanation: "At føle" means "to feel", both emotions and things you touch. To say how you feel, add mig (me): Jeg føler mig glad means "I feel happy".

sentence.da: Jeg kan **føle** vinden på min hud.
sentence.en: I can feel the wind on my skin.

at føle sig.explanation: "At føle sig" means "to feel (a certain way)" and is followed by a word like glad (happy): Jeg føler mig glad (I feel happy). Sig changes with the person: du føler dig (you feel), han føler sig (he feels).

sentence.da: Man kan **føle sig** ensom i en ny by.
sentence.en: You can feel lonely in a new city.

at føles.explanation: "At føles" means "to feel", about how something seems to you: Vandet føles koldt (The water feels cold). When a person feels, say Jeg føler mig træt (I feel tired).

sentence.da: Det kan **føles** underligt at flytte.
sentence.en: It can feel strange to move.

at følge.explanation: "At følge" means "to follow" a person, a road or a rule: Hunden følger mig (The dog follows me). It also means "to go along with", like walking someone somewhere: Jeg følger dig hjem (I will walk you home).

sentence.da: Alle skal **følge** reglerne i skolen.
sentence.en: Everyone has to follow the rules at school.

at følge med.explanation: "At følge med" means "to keep up" and "to come along": Kan du følge med? (Can you keep up?) Jeg følger med (I'll come along). Plain at følge means "to follow".

forms.en: I have kept up / come along

sentence.da: Hun går hurtigt, og jeg kan ikke **følge med**.
sentence.en: She walks fast, and I can't keep up.

at føre.explanation: "At føre" means "to lead" and "to conduct": Han fører samtalen (He is leading the conversation). It also means "to keep" accounts or records: Vi fører regnskab (We keep the accounts).

sentence.da: Vejen kan **føre** dig til stranden.
sentence.en: The road can lead you to the beach.

en fabel.explanation: "En fabel" means "a fable", a short story with a lesson, usually about animals. Æsops fabler (Aesop's fables) are the best known.

sentence.da: I en **fabel** taler dyrene som mennesker og lærer os noget.
sentence.en: In a fable the animals talk like people and teach us something.

en fabrik.explanation: "En fabrik" means "a factory", where things are made in large amounts.

sentence.da: Min bror arbejder på en **fabrik** og laver møbler.
sentence.en: My brother works at a factory and makes furniture.

en fabriksarbejder.explanation: "En fabriksarbejder" means "a factory worker", someone who works with machines or on a production line. The same pattern gives en havnearbejder (a dock worker).

sentence.da: En **fabriksarbejder** står ved et samlebånd og pakker varer.
sentence.en: A factory worker stands at an assembly line and packs goods.

en facade.explanation: "En facade" means "a facade", the front of a building, the side you see from the street. It is also used for an appearance that hides what is behind it: en facade af venlighed (a facade of friendliness).

sentence.da: Husets **facade** er gul og vender ud mod gaden.
sentence.en: The house's facade is yellow and faces the street.

en fagbog.explanation: "En fagbog" means "a nonfiction book", a book that teaches about a subject or a profession, such as medicine, law or history. Fag means a subject or trade, so a fagbog is a book for that subject.

sentence.da: Jeg læser en **fagbog** om økonomi, fordi jeg skal til eksamen.
sentence.en: I am reading a nonfiction book about economics because I have an exam.

en fagforening.explanation: "En fagforening" means "a trade union", an organization for workers in the same profession that helps with pay and contracts. Most Danish workers belong to one.

sentence.da: Min **fagforening** hjælper mig, hvis jeg får problemer på arbejdet.
sentence.en: My union helps me if I get problems at work.

en faktor.explanation: "En faktor" means "a factor", one of several things that influence a result: Prisen er en vigtig faktor (The price is an important factor). In math it also means a number that you multiply with another.

sentence.da: Vejret er en **faktor**, som man ikke selv kan styre.
sentence.en: The weather is a factor that you cannot control yourself.

en faktura.explanation: "En faktura" means "an invoice", a document a business sends to say how much you owe for goods or work. It lists what was sold and the VAT, while en regning (a bill) is the everyday word for any bill.

sentence.da: Vi sender en **faktura**, og du betaler inden fjorten dage.
sentence.en: We send an invoice, and you pay within fourteen days.

en familie.explanation: "En familie" means "a family", the people closest to you, such as parents, children, brothers and sisters.

sentence.da: Min **familie** er mor, far og søster.
sentence.en: My family is my mom, my dad and my sister.

en familiefest.explanation: "En familiefest" means "a family party", where relatives come together for a birthday or another special day.

sentence.da: Vi holder en **familiefest** for farmor.
sentence.en: We are having a family party for grandma.

en fan.explanation: "En fan" means "a fan", someone who loves a team, singer or band. For a fan that cools a room, use en ventilator (a fan).

sentence.da: Min bror er **fan** af det danske landshold.
sentence.en: My brother is a fan of the Danish national team.

en fange.explanation: "En fange" means "a prisoner", a person who is locked up in a jail or held captive. It looks like the verb at fange (to catch) and comes from the same root: the prisoner is the one who has been caught.

sentence.da: Den **fange**, der flygtede, blev fanget igen næste dag.
sentence.en: The prisoner who escaped was caught again the next day.

en fanklub.explanation: "En fanklub" means "a fan club", a group of people who support the same team, singer or other favorite. Many teams have one.

sentence.da: Hun er medlem af en **fanklub** for sit yndlingsband.
sentence.en: She is a member of a fan club for her favorite band.

en fantasi.explanation: "En fantasi" means "an imagination" or "a fantasy". It is the ability to imagine things. It is also something imagined that is not real: Det er bare en fantasi (It is just a fantasy).

sentence.da: Børn har ofte meget **fantasi**.
sentence.en: Children often have a lot of imagination.

en far.explanation: "En far" means "a father". Danish uses far for both father and dad, and children also use it as a name: Hej, far! (Hi, Dad!).

sentence.da: Min mor og min **far** har to børn.
sentence.en: My mother and my father have two children.

en farbror.explanation: "En farbror" means "an uncle", your father's brother. Your mother's brother is en morbror (an uncle).

sentence.da: Min **farbror** er min fars bror og bor i Aarhus.
sentence.en: My uncle is my father's brother and lives in Aarhus.

en fare.explanation: "En fare" means "a danger". Fare for means "danger of": Der er fare for brand (There is a danger of fire).

sentence.da: Børnene er i **fare** på den tynde is.
sentence.en: The children are in danger on the thin ice.

en farfar.explanation: "En farfar" means "a grandfather" on your father's side. It is built from far (father) and far (father): father's father. On your mother's side he is en morfar (mother's father).

sentence.da: Min **farfar** er min fars far.
sentence.en: My grandfather is my father's father.

en farmaceut.explanation: "En farmaceut" means "a pharmacist", a person with a university degree who works in a pharmacy and knows about drugs. A farmakonom (a pharmacy technician) has a shorter education and also works there.

sentence.da: En **farmaceut** kan forklare, hvordan man tager sin medicin.
sentence.en: A pharmacist can explain how to take your medicine.

en farmor.explanation: "En farmor" means "a grandmother" on your father's side. It is built from far (father) and mor (mother): father's mother. You can call her farmor directly: Farmor kommer i dag (Grandma is coming today).

sentence.da: Min **farmor** er min fars mor.
sentence.en: My grandmother is my father's mother.

en fart.explanation: "En fart" means "a speed", how quickly something moves. It is also used for pace and energy: Der er fart på (Things are really moving).

sentence.da: Bilen kørte i høj **fart** gennem byen.
sentence.en: The car drove at high speed through the town.

en fartbøde.explanation: "En fartbøde" means "a speeding ticket", the fine for driving too fast. It is built from fart (speed) and bøde (fine). Bøde can stand alone: Jeg fik en bøde (I got a fine).

sentence.da: Han fik en **fartbøde** på motorvejen.
sentence.en: He got a speeding ticket on the highway.

en fartgrænse.explanation: "En fartgrænse" means "a speed limit". If you go too fast, you break it: at overskride fartgrænsen (to exceed the speed limit).

sentence.da: Der er en **fartgrænse** på 50 i byen.
sentence.en: There is a speed limit of 50 in town.

en farve.explanation: "En farve" means "a color", the look of something that you can name, such as the shade of a shirt or a wall.

sentence.da: Hvilken **farve** har din bil? Den er rød.
sentence.en: What color is your car? It is red.

en fase.explanation: "En fase" means "a phase", a part of a process or of someone's life that has its own character and later ends.

sentence.da: Barnet er i en svær **fase** lige nu.
sentence.en: The child is in a hard phase right now.

en fastelavnsbolle.explanation: "En fastelavnsbolle" means "a Shrovetide bun", a sweet bun with cream and icing that Danes eat around Fastelavn, a February holiday when children dress up in costumes.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en **fastelavnsbolle** med fløde.
sentence.en: I am eating a Shrovetide bun with cream.

en faster.explanation: "En faster" means "an aunt", your father's sister. Your mother's sister is en moster (an aunt).

sentence.da: Min **faster** er min fars søster og bor i Aalborg.
sentence.en: My aunt is my father's sister and lives in Aalborg.

en favorit.explanation: "En favorit" means "a favorite", the one you like best. It also starts compounds like favoritmad (favorite food).

sentence.da: Pizza er min **favorit** blandt alle retter.
sentence.en: Pizza is my favorite of all dishes.

en feber.explanation: "En feber" means "a fever", a high body temperature when you are sick. Danes say Jeg har feber (I have a fever), usually without en.

sentence.da: Hun har **feber** og bliver i sengen.
sentence.en: She has a fever and stays in bed.

en fejebakke.explanation: "En fejebakke" means "a dustpan", the small flat tray you sweep dust into. It is built from at feje (to sweep) and en bakke (a tray). En bakke also means "a hill", as in en stor bakke (a big hill).

sentence.da: Jeg samler støvet op med en **fejebakke**.
sentence.en: I pick up the dust with a dustpan.

en fejl.explanation: "En fejl" means "an error" or "a bug", and also "a mistake": Der er en fejl i programmet (There is an error in the program). Jeg lavede en fejl (I made a mistake).

sentence.da: Jeg fandt en **fejl** i din tekst.
sentence.en: I found a mistake in your text.

en fejltagelse.explanation: "En fejltagelse" means "a mistake", usually something you did or believed wrongly by accident. For a fault in a machine or a text, use en fejl (an error).

sentence.da: Det var en **fejltagelse**, at jeg sendte mailen til dig.
sentence.en: It was a mistake that I sent the email to you.

en fejring.explanation: "En fejring" means "a celebration", the act of celebrating an event, usually followed by af (of) and the occasion: fejringen af jul (the celebration of Christmas). For the party itself, en fest (a party) is the usual word.

sentence.da: Familien holder en lille **fejring** af hendes fødselsdag.
sentence.en: The family holds a small celebration of her birthday.

en ferie.explanation: "En ferie" means "a vacation" or holiday, a time away from work or school. You say på ferie (on vacation). I ferien means "during the vacation".

sentence.da: Jeg har fri og tager på **ferie**.
sentence.en: I have time off and am going on vacation.

en fersken.explanation: "En fersken" means "a peach", a round fruit with soft, fuzzy skin.

sentence.da: En **fersken** er sød og saftig, og den har en sten.
sentence.en: A peach is sweet and juicy, and it has a pit.

en fest.explanation: "En fest" means "a party" or a celebration. You say at holde fest (to have a party) or at gå til fest (to go to a party). God fest! means "Have a good party!".

sentence.da: Vi holder **fest** med musik og kage.
sentence.en: We are having a party with music and cake.

en festdag.explanation: "En festdag" means "a festive day", a day that is celebrated, such as Christmas Eve or a confirmation day. It is not the same as en helligdag (a public holiday), which is a day when most people do not work.

sentence.da: Bryllupsdagen er en stor **festdag** for hele familien.
sentence.en: The wedding day is a big festive day for the whole family.

en festival.explanation: "En festival" means "a festival", usually for music or film.

sentence.da: Vi skal på **festival** i sommer og sove i telt.
sentence.en: We are going to a festival this summer and sleeping in a tent.

en festsal.explanation: "En festsal" means "a banquet hall", a big room for parties, weddings and school events.

sentence.da: Bryllupsgæsterne spiser og danser i den store **festsal**.
sentence.en: The wedding guests eat and dance in the big banquet hall.

en festtale.explanation: "En festtale" means "a celebratory speech", given by someone at a party. It is built from fest (party) and tale (speech). Danish uses at holde (to hold) for giving a speech: at holde en tale (to give a speech).

sentence.da: Hun holdt en kort **festtale** for sin bedste ven.
sentence.en: She gave a short speech for her best friend.

en fiasko.explanation: "En fiasko" means "a failure", a plan or event that goes badly wrong in a big, public way. It is stronger than a small mistake: a whole project or show can be en fiasko.

sentence.da: Festen blev en **fiasko**, fordi maden slet ikke kom.
sentence.en: The party became a fiasco because the food never came.

en figur.explanation: "En figur" means "a figure", such as a shape, a drawing or a character in a story: en figur i bogen (a character in the book). It also means a person's body shape: Hun har en flot figur (She has a nice figure).

sentence.da: Børnene tegner en sjov **figur** på papiret.
sentence.en: The children draw a funny figure on the paper.

en fil.explanation: "En fil" means "a file" on a computer. It is also a metal tool for smoothing things, like en neglefil (a nail file).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke åbne den **fil**, du sendte mig.
sentence.en: I cannot open the file you sent me.

en filial.explanation: "En filial" means "a branch", a local part of a bigger company, set up in another town. It has its own staff, but it belongs to the company and follows its rules.

sentence.da: Banken har en **filial** i hver større by.
sentence.en: The bank has a branch in every larger town.

en film.explanation: "En film" means "a film" or "a movie". More than one is also "film": to film means two films (to is the number two). At se en film means "to watch a film".

sentence.da: Vi ser en **film** i biografen.
sentence.en: We watch a film at the cinema.

en filmaften.explanation: "En filmaften" means "a movie night", a night in watching films, often at home with friends. I aften means "tonight", as in Skal vi have filmaften i aften? (Shall we have movie night tonight?)

sentence.da: Vi har **filmaften** hver fredag med popcorn og venner.
sentence.en: We have a movie night every Friday with popcorn and friends.

en filmstjerne.explanation: "En filmstjerne" means "a film star", a famous person from the movies. It is built from film (movie) and stjerne (star). Stjerne is also a star in the sky: Der er mange stjerner i aften (There are many stars tonight).

sentence.da: Hun er blevet en kendt **filmstjerne** i USA.
sentence.en: She has become a famous film star in the USA.

en filosof.explanation: "En filosof" means "a philosopher", a person who thinks deeply about big questions, such as what truth is and how people should live.

sentence.da: En **filosof** tænker over, hvad der er rigtigt og forkert.
sentence.en: A philosopher thinks about what is right and wrong.

en finale.explanation: "En finale" means "a final", the last match or round that decides who wins a competition. It is also the big last part of a show or a concert.

sentence.da: Kampen søndag er en **finale**, og alle vil se den.
sentence.en: The match on Sunday is a final, and everyone wants to watch it.

en finanslov.explanation: "En finanslov" means "a national budget" or "a Finance Act", the law that the Danish parliament (Folketinget) passes each year to decide how the state gets and spends money. It is a real law, not just a plan.

sentence.da: Folketinget skal vedtage en **finanslov**, før det nye år begynder.
sentence.en: Parliament must pass a finance act before the new year begins.

en finger.explanation: "En finger" means "a finger". The thumb is tommelfinger and the index finger is pegefinger. Danish says the finger where English says my finger: Jeg har ondt i fingeren means "I have a pain in the finger", i.e., my finger hurts.

sentence.da: Hun har en ring på sin **finger**.
sentence.en: She has a ring on her finger.

en finne.explanation: "En finne" means "a fin", the flat part on a fish or a dolphin that helps it swim and steer.

sentence.da: Fisken bruger sin **finne** til at dreje i vandet.
sentence.en: The fish uses its fin to turn in the water.

en firewall.explanation: "En firewall" means "a firewall", a protection that blocks unwanted visitors on a computer or an internet connection.

sentence.da: Min **firewall** stopper farlige programmer.
sentence.en: My firewall stops dangerous programs.

en firkant.explanation: "En firkant" means "a four-sided shape", built from fire (four) and kant (edge). It is any shape with four sides, like a rectangle, while et kvadrat (a square) has four equal sides.

sentence.da: Bordet er en **firkant**, ikke en cirkel.
sentence.en: The table is a four-sided shape, not a circle.

en fisk.explanation: "En fisk" means "a fish", both the animal in the water and the food on your plate. The plural can be the same word as the single one: tre fisk (three fish).

sentence.da: En **fisk** svømmer i vandet.
sentence.en: A fish swims in the water.

en fiskefrikadelle.explanation: "En fiskefrikadelle" means "a fish cake", a flat patty of fish that is often eaten with remoulade (a tangy sauce) and a slice of lemon.

sentence.da: En **fiskefrikadelle** er lavet af hakket fisk og stegt på panden.
sentence.en: A fish cake is made of minced fish and fried in a pan.

en fiskehandler.explanation: "En fiskehandler" means "a fishmonger", the person who sells fresh fish. The word also means the shop itself, so you buy fish hos (at) fiskehandleren.

sentence.da: Jeg køber frisk laks hos en **fiskehandler**.
sentence.en: I buy fresh salmon from a fishmonger.

en fisker.explanation: "En fisker" means "a fisherman", someone who catches fish as a job. The same word is used for men and women.

sentence.da: Vores nabo er **fisker** og sejler hver morgen.
sentence.en: Our neighbor is a fisherman and sails every morning.

en fiskerby.explanation: "En fiskerby" means "a fishing village", a small community by the sea where people make their living from fishing.

sentence.da: Jeg bor i en lille **fiskerby** ved havet.
sentence.en: I live in a small fishing village by the sea.

en fiskestang.explanation: "En fiskestang" means "a fishing rod", the long, thin pole you hold when you fish. The ending stang (a pole) also appears in en flagstang (a flagpole).

sentence.da: Han fanger fisk med en **fiskestang** og en lille krog.
sentence.en: He catches fish with a fishing rod and a small hook.
