et fundament.explanation: "Et fundament" means "a foundation", the solid structure under a building that carries its weight. It is also used for what something rests on, such as trust in a friendship.

sentence.da: Huset står på et stærkt **fundament** af beton.
sentence.en: The house stands on a strong foundation of concrete.

et fyrretræ.explanation: "Et fyrretræ" means "a pine tree", a tall evergreen tree that grows well on sandy soil and is common in Danish forests.

sentence.da: Et **fyrretræ** har nåle i stedet for blade og er grønt hele året.
sentence.en: A pine tree has needles instead of leaves and is green all year.

et fyrtårn.explanation: "Et fyrtårn" means "a lighthouse", a tall tower with a bright light that guides ships. It is built from fyr (beacon light) and tårn (tower). Fyr also means a guy: Han er en flot fyr (He is a handsome guy).

sentence.da: Om natten viser et **fyrtårn** skibene vej.
sentence.en: At night, a lighthouse shows the ships the way.

et får.explanation: "Et får" means "a sheep". Do not mix it up with får from at få (to get): Han får en gave means "He gets a gift".

sentence.da: Et **får** har uld og siger mæh.
sentence.en: A sheep has wool and says baa.

et fællesskab.explanation: "Et fællesskab" means "a community", a group bound together by something shared, and the feeling of belonging that comes with it. For the people living in one local area, Danes say et lokalsamfund (a local community).

sentence.da: I vores **fællesskab** hjælper alle hinanden, når nogen har brug for det.
sentence.en: In our community everyone helps each other when someone needs it.

et fællesvaskeri.explanation: "Et fællesvaskeri" means "a shared laundry room", where all the residents of a building wash their clothes. Fælles means shared: Vi har et fælles køkken (We have a shared kitchen).

sentence.da: Der er et **fællesvaskeri** i huset, som alle bruger.
sentence.en: There is a shared laundry room in the building that everyone uses.

et fængsel.explanation: "Et fængsel" means "a prison", the building. To be in prison is to sidde i fængsel, without et: Han sidder i fængsel (He is in prison).

sentence.da: Han kom i **fængsel** i to år.
sentence.en: He went to prison for two years.

et fænomen.explanation: "Et fænomen" means "a phenomenon", something that can be seen or noticed, especially something unusual or hard to explain, such as a rainbow or a new trend. With natur (nature) in front, et naturfænomen is a natural phenomenon.

sentence.da: Nordlys er et smukt **fænomen**, men man ser det sjældent i Danmark.
sentence.en: The northern lights are a beautiful phenomenon, but you rarely see them in Denmark.

et fødested.explanation: "Et fødested" means "a birthplace", the town or country where someone was born. It is made of at føde (to give birth) and et sted (a place). You will see Fødested as a box on forms.

sentence.da: Mit **fødested** er Odense.
sentence.en: My birthplace is Odense.

et føl.explanation: "Et føl" means "a foal", a young horse or donkey that still drinks its mother's milk.

sentence.da: Hoppen står i engen med sit lille **føl**.
sentence.en: The mare stands in the meadow with her little foal.

faglig.explanation: "Faglig" means "professional" or "academic", about a subject or a trade. It describes knowledge and skills in that field: faglig viden (knowledge of the field). It also covers the trade union side of work, as in fagforening (trade union).

sentence.da: Rapporten er meget **faglig** og bygger på forskning.
sentence.en: The report is very professional and builds on research.

faktisk.explanation: "Faktisk" means "actually" or "in fact". Use it when the truth is a bit different from what someone thinks: Det er faktisk nemt (It is actually easy).

sentence.da: Nej, han er **faktisk** dansk.
sentence.en: No, he is actually Danish.

falsk.explanation: "Falsk" means "fake", for things made to look real. For a person it means someone who only pretends to be nice: en falsk ven (a false friend).

sentence.da: Sedlen er **falsk**, og banken tager ikke imod den.
sentence.en: The bill is fake, and the bank will not accept it.

fantasifuld.explanation: "Fantasifuld" means "imaginative", full of ideas and imagination, for a person or for something made by one. The ending -fuld means full of, and works the same in smertefuld (painful).

sentence.da: Hun er så **fantasifuld**, at hun finder på nye eventyr hver dag.
sentence.en: She is so imaginative that she makes up new adventures every day.

fantastisk.explanation: "Fantastisk" means "fantastic". It is stronger than god (good), so save it for something really great.

sentence.da: Maden var **fantastisk**!
sentence.en: The food was fantastic!

farlig.explanation: "Farlig" means "dangerous" and comes from fare (danger). Livsfarlig means "life-threatening".

sentence.da: Vejen er meget **farlig**.
sentence.en: The road is very dangerous.

farvel.explanation: "Farvel" means "goodbye". Danes often use hej hej (bye bye) or vi ses (see you) for everyday goodbyes, while farvel sounds more final.

sentence.da: Jeg siger **farvel** til min ven.
sentence.en: I say goodbye to my friend.

farverig.explanation: "Farverig" means "colorful", with many bright colors. It also describes a person or a story that is lively and out of the ordinary: en farverig person (a colorful person).

sentence.da: Gaden er **farverig**, fordi husene er malet gule, røde og blå.
sentence.en: The street is colorful because the houses are painted yellow, red and blue.

fascinerende.explanation: "Fascinerende" means "fascinating", something that holds your attention and does not let go. For how you feel, use fascineret: Jeg er fascineret (I am fascinated).

sentence.da: Fuglenes liv er **fascinerende**, og jeg læser om dem.
sentence.en: The life of birds is fascinating, and I read about them.

fast.explanation: "Fast" means "fixed", for things that stay the same: en fast pris (a fixed price). It also means "steady" or "lasting": et fast job (a steady job).

sentence.da: Vi har en **fast** tid hver uge.
sentence.en: We have a set time every week.

fastelavn.explanation: "Fastelavn" means "Shrovetide", a holiday in late winter, in the days before Lent, when a barrel full of sweets is hit open.

forms.en: hit the cat out of the barrel

sentence.da: Børnene klæder sig ud til **fastelavn** og får slik.
sentence.en: The children dress up for Shrovetide and get candy.

fattig.explanation: "Fattig" means "poor", with little money, for people and also for countries. Stakkels also means "poor", but in the sense of unlucky: stakkels dig means "poor you".

sentence.da: Han er **fattig** og har næsten ingen penge.
sentence.en: He is poor and has almost no money.

fattigdom.explanation: "Fattigdom" means "poverty", the state of being poor. It is built from fattig (poor). The ending -dom also makes en sygdom (an illness) from syg (sick).

sentence.da: Mange børn lever i **fattigdom**.
sentence.en: Many children live in poverty.

februar.explanation: "Februar" means "February". Month names are written with a small letter: i februar (in February).

sentence.da: Efter januar kommer **februar**.
sentence.en: After January comes February.

fed.explanation: "Fed" means "cool" in casual speech: Det er fedt! (That is cool!) It also means "fat", as in fed mad (fatty food).

sentence.da: Wow, du har en **fed** cykel!
sentence.en: Wow, you have a cool bike!

fedt.explanation: "Fedt" means "fat", the kind in food. In casual talk it also means "cool": Det er fedt! (That is cool!)

sentence.da: Der er meget **fedt** i pommes frites.
sentence.en: There is a lot of fat in french fries.

fej.explanation: "Fej" means "cowardly", for someone who lacks courage when it counts. It judges a person's character, while bange (afraid) is only a feeling: Jeg er bange, men jeg er ikke fej (I am afraid, but I am not cowardly).

sentence.da: Han er **fej**, fordi han altid løber væk.
sentence.en: He is cowardly because he always runs away.

fejhed.explanation: "En fejhed" means "cowardice", a lack of nerve when you should act or stand up for something: Han tav af fejhed (He kept quiet out of cowardice).

sentence.da: Det var **fejhed** at lade andre tage skylden.
sentence.en: It was cowardice to let others take the blame.

fejlfri.explanation: "Fejlfri" means "flawless" or "without mistakes". It is built from fejl (mistake) and fri (free). The same -fri is in sukkerfri (sugar-free).

sentence.da: Teksten er **fejlfri**, og der er ingen stavefejl.
sentence.en: The text is flawless, and there are no spelling mistakes.

fem.explanation: "Fem" means "five". Fifty is not "femti" but halvtreds (fifty).

sentence.da: Jeg har **fem** fingre på hver hånd.
sentence.en: I have five fingers on each hand.

femogtredive.explanation: "Femogtredive" means "thirty-five". Danish says the five first: fem-og-tredive is literally five-and-thirty. The same goes for 25, femogtyve (five-and-twenty), and 45, femogfyrre (five-and-forty).

sentence.da: Min bror er **femogtredive** år.
sentence.en: My brother is thirty-five years old.

femte.explanation: "Femte" means "fifth" and is used for order and dates: den femte marts (the fifth of March). Fem is the plain number: fem dage (five days), but den femte dag (the fifth day).

sentence.da: Min fødselsdag er den **femte** marts.
sentence.en: My birthday is the fifth of March.

femten.explanation: "Femten" means "fifteen". Danes also say en kvart (a quarter of an hour) for fifteen minutes.

sentence.da: Der er **femten** elever i klassen.
sentence.en: There are fifteen students in the class.

festlig.explanation: "Festlig" means "festive", for something that feels like a celebration. It can also mean "amusing": Det var da festligt! (Well, that was amusing!)

sentence.da: Julen er **festlig**, fordi vi spiser og synger sammen.
sentence.en: Christmas is festive because we eat and sing together.

feta.explanation: "Feta" means "feta", a white, salty cheese from Greece that crumbles easily.

sentence.da: Salaten smager godt med salt **feta** og agurk.
sentence.en: The salad tastes good with salty feta and cucumber.

fibre.explanation: "Fibre" means "fibers", the thin parts that plants, muscles and cloth are made of. In food, they help digestion, and Danes call that kostfibre (dietary fiber).

sentence.da: Fuldkornsbrød indeholder mange **fibre**, som er gode for maven.
sentence.en: Whole-grain bread contains many fibers that are good for the stomach.

fiktiv.explanation: "Fiktiv" means "fictional", invented rather than found in life, like a character in a book. It is also used for things invented to look genuine: en fiktiv adresse (a fake address).

sentence.da: Romanens hovedperson er **fiktiv**, men byen findes i virkeligheden.
sentence.en: The main character of the novel is fictional, but the city exists in reality.

filosofi.explanation: "Filosofi" means "philosophy", asking big questions about life, truth and what is right. It also means one person's view of how to live or work: Min filosofi er at tage én dag ad gangen (My philosophy is to take one day at a time).

sentence.da: Hun studerer **filosofi** og spørger, hvorfor vi findes.
sentence.en: She studies philosophy and asks why we exist.

fin.explanation: "Fin" means "fine" or "nice". It can also mean "fancy" or "elegant": en fin restaurant means "a fancy restaurant". Fint! on its own means "Great!" or "Okay, good!".

sentence.da: Solen skinner på en **fin** dag.
sentence.en: The sun shines on a nice day.

finland.explanation: "Finland" means "Finland", the Nordic country known for its thousands of lakes. Its capital is Helsinki.

sentence.da: **Finland** ligger øst for Sverige.
sentence.en: Finland lies east of Sweden.

finsk.explanation: "Finsk" means "Finnish" and describes things from Finland, including the language. It is written with a small letter, even for the language: Jeg taler finsk means "I speak Finnish".

sentence.da: Han kommer fra Finland og taler **finsk**.
sentence.en: He comes from Finland and speaks Finnish.

fint.explanation: "Fint" means "fine" or "nicely". It is a common answer to Hvordan går det? (How is it going?): Det går fint (It is going fine). Alone, Fint! means "Fine!" and agrees with a plan: Skal vi mødes klokken tre? Fint! (Shall we meet at three? Fine!).

sentence.da: Hvordan går det? Det går **fint**.
sentence.en: How is it going? It is going fine.

fire.explanation: "Fire" means "four": fire kroner (four kroner). Don't mix it up with fyrre (forty), which looks similar: fyrre kroner (forty kroner).

sentence.da: Hunden har **fire** ben.
sentence.en: The dog has four legs.

fireogtyve.explanation: "Fireogtyve" means "twenty-four". Danish says the four first: fire-og-tyve is literally four-and-twenty. The same goes for 25, femogtyve (five-and-twenty), and 26, seksogtyve (six-and-twenty).

sentence.da: Der er **fireogtyve** timer i et døgn.
sentence.en: There are twenty-four hours in a day.

firkantet.explanation: "Firkantet" means "square-shaped", for anything with four corners, not only a perfect square. The exact word for a perfect square is kvadratisk. It also describes a rigid person: Han er meget firkantet (He is very rigid).

sentence.da: Skakbrættet er **firkantet** og har 64 felter.
sentence.en: The chessboard is square-shaped and has 64 squares.

firs.explanation: "Firs" means "eighty". It is short for firsindstyve (four times twenty). Sixty works the same way: tres (sixty) is three twenties.

sentence.da: Min bedstefar er **firs** år gammel.
sentence.en: My grandfather is eighty years old.

fiskeri.explanation: "Fiskeri" means "fishing" as a trade or industry. For a hobby, Danes say lystfiskeri (angling).

sentence.da: Mange familier i den lille havneby lever af **fiskeri**.
sentence.en: Many families in the small port town live from fishing.

fitness.explanation: "Fitness" means "fitness" in the sense of gym training. The place itself is et fitnesscenter (a gym). Being in good shape is not fitness in Danish, but i form (in shape).

sentence.da: Jeg dyrker **fitness** hver morgen før arbejde.
sentence.en: I do fitness every morning before work.

fjendtlig.explanation: "Fjendtlig" means "hostile", showing that you want to oppose or harm someone. It is built from en fjende (an enemy), and it also means belonging to the enemy in a war.

sentence.da: Hunden var **fjendtlig** og knurrede af os.
sentence.en: The dog was hostile and growled at us.

fjerde.explanation: "Fjerde" means "fourth" and is used for order and dates: den fjerde maj (the fourth of May). Fire is the plain number: fire dage (four days), but den fjerde dag (the fourth day).

sentence.da: Han sad i **fjerde** række.
sentence.en: He sat in the fourth row.

fjerkræ.explanation: "Fjerkræ" means "poultry", the group name for farm birds, and for their meat in a shop. It is built from fjer (a feather) and an old word kræ (a creature).

sentence.da: Man holder **fjerkræ** på gården for kød og æg.
sentence.en: You keep poultry on the farm for meat and eggs.

fjern.explanation: "Fjern" means "distant" or "remote", for places and times far away. It is also the start of fjernsyn (TV), literally a far-away view.

sentence.da: Han er en **fjern** fætter til mig.
sentence.en: He is a distant cousin of mine.

fjernvarme.explanation: "Fjernvarme" means "district heating", hot water made at one central place and sent to many homes. It is built from fjern (far) and varme (warmth): warmth from far away.

sentence.da: Med **fjernvarme** kommer varmen i rør fra et stort værk.
sentence.en: With district heating, the warmth comes in pipes from a big plant.

fjollet.explanation: "Fjollet" means "silly", playful and not serious: Stop med at være så fjollet (Stop being so silly). It is not harsh, so you can say it to a friend or a child.

sentence.da: Hun er **fjollet** og laver sjove grimasser.
sentence.en: She is silly and makes funny faces.

fjorten.explanation: "Fjorten" means "fourteen". Danes say fjorten dage (fourteen days) for "two weeks": Vi ses om fjorten dage (See you in two weeks).

sentence.da: Vi tager på ferie i **fjorten** dage.
sentence.en: We are going on vacation for fourteen days.

flad.explanation: "Flad" means "flat", with no bumps: Danmark er fladt (Denmark is flat). It also fits a tire with no air: Mit dæk er fladt (My tire is flat).

sentence.da: Stenen er **flad** og glat som en tallerken.
sentence.en: The stone is flat and smooth like a plate.

fleksibel.explanation: "Fleksibel" means "flexible" and describes a plan or a person that can change easily: Jeg er fleksibel i weekenden (I am flexible on the weekend). The opposite is stiv (stiff).

sentence.da: Min chef er **fleksibel** og lader mig arbejde hjemme.
sentence.en: My boss is flexible and lets me work from home.

fleksibilitet.explanation: "Fleksibilitet" means "flexibility", being able to bend or adapt, both for a body and for a plan or a workplace: Dansere har brug for fleksibilitet i kroppen (Dancers need flexibility in the body).

sentence.da: Hjemmearbejde giver mig **fleksibilitet**, fordi jeg selv bestemmer min tid.
sentence.en: Working from home gives me flexibility because I decide my own time.

flere.explanation: "Flere" means "more" or "several", for things you can count one by one: Jeg vil have flere kager (I want more cakes). For something you can't count, use mere: Jeg vil have mere kage (I want more cake), mere vand (more water).

sentence.da: Der er **flere** æbler end pærer i kurven.
sentence.en: There are more apples than pears in the basket.

flink.explanation: "Flink" means "kind" or "nice", for a helpful person: Han er flink (He is nice). With til, it means "good at": Hun er flink til matematik (She is good at math).

sentence.da: Naboen er **flink**, og han hjælper os ofte.
sentence.en: The neighbor is nice, and he often helps us.

flittig.explanation: "Flittig" means "diligent" and describes someone who works hard and steadily. The opposite is doven (lazy).

sentence.da: Hun er **flittig** og læser lektier hver dag.
sentence.en: She is diligent and does homework every day.

flormelis.explanation: "Flormelis" means "powdered sugar", very fine white sugar for icing and for dusting on cakes. It is built from flor (a thin veil) and melis (a kind of sugar).

sentence.da: Drys kagen med **flormelis**, så den ligner sne.
sentence.en: Dust the cake with powdered sugar so that it looks like snow.

flot.explanation: "Flot" means "good-looking" or "impressive", for people, clothes, places and even results. Saying Flot! to someone means "Well done!".

sentence.da: Hun er smuk og har en **flot** kjole.
sentence.en: She is beautiful and has a nice-looking dress.

flov.explanation: "Flov" means "embarrassed", how you feel after a slip: Hun følte sig flov (She felt embarrassed). It describes you, not the situation. The situation is pinlig (embarrassing): Det var pinligt (That was embarrassing).

sentence.da: Jeg blev **flov**, da jeg glemte hans navn.
sentence.en: I got embarrassed when I forgot his name.

flovhed.explanation: "En flovhed" means "embarrassment", the uncomfortable feeling after you did something silly in front of others. It comes from flov (sheepish).

sentence.da: Hun rødmede af **flovhed** foran hele klassen.
sentence.en: She blushed with embarrassment in front of the whole class.

flydende.explanation: "Flydende" means "fluent" for speaking, and "liquid" for things you can pour. It is the same picture in both: speech or liquid that runs smoothly without stopping.

sentence.da: Efter to år taler hun **flydende** dansk.
sentence.en: After two years she speaks fluent Danish.

flæsk.explanation: "Flæsk" means "pork belly", fatty slices of pork, often fried. It is the main part of stegt flæsk med persillesovs (fried pork belly with parsley sauce), a classic Danish dish.

sentence.da: Fede skiver **flæsk** bliver sprøde, når man steger dem.
sentence.en: Fatty slices of pork belly become crisp when you fry them.

flæskesteg.explanation: "Flæskesteg" means "roast pork", a pork roast with crispy skin. It is built from flæsk (fatty pork) and en steg (a roast). En steg is any roast: en oksesteg (a beef roast).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **flæskesteg** med kartofler og sovs.
sentence.en: We eat roast pork with potatoes and gravy.

fløde.explanation: "Fløde" means "cream", the fatty part of milk, used in coffee, sauces and desserts. Piskefløde means "whipping cream" and is made of piske (to whip) and "fløde".

sentence.da: Vil du have **fløde** i kaffen?
sentence.en: Do you want cream in your coffee?

flødeost.explanation: "Flødeost" means "cream cheese", a soft white cheese for bread or cooking. It is fløde (cream) and ost (cheese) joined together.

sentence.da: Vi spiser brød med **flødeost** og laks.
sentence.en: We eat bread with cream cheese and salmon.

fn.explanation: "FN" means "the UN", short for Forenede Nationer (United Nations). It is said letter by letter: ef-en.

sentence.da: **FN** arbejder for fred og hjælper mennesker i krigsramte lande.
sentence.en: The UN works for peace and helps people in war-torn countries.

fodbold.explanation: "Fodbold" means "soccer". The game has no en in front: Jeg spiller fodbold means "I play soccer". En fodbold is the ball.

sentence.da: Børnene spiller **fodbold** og sparker til bolden.
sentence.en: The children play soccer and kick the ball.

folketinget.explanation: "Folketinget" means "the Danish Parliament", where the country's laws are made. For another country's parliament, say et parlament (a parliament).

sentence.da: **Folketinget** stemmer om den nye lov i dag.
sentence.en: The Parliament votes on the new law today.

for.explanation: "For" means "for", "too" or "ago", depending on the sentence. Compare Suppen er varm (The soup is hot) with Suppen er for varm (The soup is too hot). With siden (ago), it counts back in time: for to dage siden (two days ago). For a gift, Danish usually says til: en gave til dig (a gift for you).

sentence.da: Suppen er **for** varm.
sentence.en: The soup is too hot.

for det meste.explanation: "For det meste" means "mostly" and says that something is true in most cases. It is close to som regel (usually).

forms.da: Det er for det meste rart vejr.
Jeg læser for det meste om aftenen.
forms.en: I mostly read in the evening.

sentence.da: Vi spiser **for det meste** hjemme, men nogle gange ude.
sentence.en: We mostly eat at home, but sometimes out.

for eksempel.explanation: "For eksempel" means "for example". It goes right before the example: Jeg spiser meget frugt, for eksempel bananer (I eat a lot of fruit, for example bananas). In writing it is often shortened to fx (e.g.).

forms.da: Jeg kan godt lide frugt, for eksempel æbler.
forms.en: I like fruit, for example apples.

forms.da: Vi kan mødes, for eksempel i morgen.
forms.en: We can meet, for example tomorrow.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser frugt, **for eksempel** æbler.
sentence.en: I eat fruit, for example apples.

for evigt.explanation: "For evigt" means "forever", with no end. For a long wait, say Det tager en evighed (It takes forever).

sentence.da: Jeg vil huske dette sted **for evigt**.
sentence.en: I will remember this place forever.

for længe siden.explanation: "For længe siden" means "a long time ago": Han var her for længe siden (He was here a long time ago). Put a number in place of længe (long) to say exactly how long: for to år siden (two years ago).

forms.en: We met a long time ago
That was a long time ago

forms.da: Jeg boede der for længe siden
forms.en: I lived there a long time ago

sentence.da: Vi boede i Odense **for længe siden**.
sentence.en: We lived in Odense a long time ago.

for nylig.explanation: "For nylig" means "recently". It looks like for tiden (at the moment), but it points to the past, not to now.

forms.da: Jeg har for nylig købt en cykel
Vi har for nylig mødt ham

sentence.da: Jeg har **for nylig** købt en ny cykel.
sentence.en: I recently bought a new bike.

for pokker.explanation: "For pokker" means "darn it" or "for heaven's sake". It is a mild thing to say when something annoying or surprising happens.

forms.da: For pokker, jeg har glemt nøglen!
forms.en: Darn it, I forgot the key!

sentence.da: **For pokker**, jeg har glemt nøglen!
sentence.en: Darn it, I forgot the key!

for søren.explanation: "For søren" means "oh dear" or "goodness" and shows surprise or mild annoyance.

forms.da: For søren, er klokken allerede otte?

sentence.da: **For søren**, hvor er det varmt i dag!
sentence.en: Goodness, it is so hot today!

for tiden.explanation: "For tiden" means "at the moment" or "these days", for something that is true now but may change. For this very second, say lige nu (right now).

forms.da: Jeg bor i Aarhus for tiden
forms.en: I live in Aarhus at the moment
She works from home at the moment
These days it rains a lot

sentence.da: Jeg arbejder hjemme **for tiden**.
sentence.en: I am working from home at the moment.

foran.explanation: "Foran" means "in front of". Compare Jeg står foran døren (I stand in front of the door) with Jeg står bag døren (I stand behind the door). Før (before) is only for time, not place: før klokken fem (before five o'clock).

sentence.da: Bilen holder **foran** huset.
sentence.en: The car is parked in front of the house.

forbavset.explanation: "Forbavset" means "astonished", a strong feeling of being taken aback by something unexpected. It is used with over: forbavset over resultatet (astonished at the result).

sentence.da: Hun blev **forbavset**, da hun så gaven.
sentence.en: She was astonished when she saw the gift.

forbi.explanation: "Forbi" means "past" or "by". Han gik forbi huset means "He walked past the house" (he did not stop). It also means "over": Sommeren er forbi (The summer is over). Kom forbi i aften! means "Drop by tonight!".

sentence.da: Bussen kører **forbi** skolen.
sentence.en: The bus drives past the school.

forbløffende.explanation: "Forbløffende" means "astonishing", and it describes the thing itself, not the person who reacts: Resultatet er forbløffende (The result is astonishing). For the person, use forbavset (astonished).

sentence.da: Det er **forbløffende**, hvor hurtigt barnet lærer at læse.
sentence.en: It is astonishing how fast the child learns to read.

forbløffet.explanation: "Forbløffet" means "amazed", so taken aback that you hardly know what to say. It often goes with over (at): forbløffet over resultatet (amazed at the result).

sentence.da: Publikum var **forbløffet**, da tryllekunstneren forsvandt.
sentence.en: The audience was amazed when the magician disappeared.

forbrug.explanation: "Forbrug" means "consumption", how much of something, such as fuel or food, gets used up. The matching verb is at forbruge (to consume).

sentence.da: Vores **forbrug** af strøm er højt om vinteren, fordi det er koldt.
sentence.en: Our use of electricity is high in winter because it is cold.

forbudt.explanation: "Forbudt" means "forbidden", for things the rules do not allow: Rygning er forbudt (Smoking is not allowed).

sentence.da: Det er **forbudt** at køre her.
sentence.en: It is forbidden to drive here.

fordelagtig.explanation: "Fordelagtig" means "advantageous", giving you a gain or a better position. It is typically used about prices, deals and conditions, and is built from fordel (an advantage).

sentence.da: Banken tilbyder en meget **fordelagtig** rente.
sentence.en: The bank offers a very advantageous interest rate.

fordi.explanation: "Fordi" means "because". It answers Hvorfor? (Why?): Hvorfor er du træt? (Why are you tired?) - Fordi jeg sover for lidt (Because I sleep too little). Do not mix it up with derfor (that is why): Jeg er træt, derfor går jeg i seng (I am tired, that is why I go to bed).

sentence.da: Jeg bliver hjemme **fordi** jeg er syg.
sentence.en: I stay home because I am sick.

fordomsfri.explanation: "Fordomsfri" means "unbiased", without fixed opinions about people before you know them. It is built from en fordom (a prejudice) and fri (free).

sentence.da: Hun er **fordomsfri** og møder alle med et åbent sind.
sentence.en: She is unbiased and meets everyone with an open mind.

fordomsfuld.explanation: "Fordomsfuld" means "prejudiced", judging people or things by a fixed opinion formed before you know them. It is made of fordom (a prejudice) and -fuld (full of).

sentence.da: Man bør ikke være **fordomsfuld** over for nye naboer.
sentence.en: You should not be prejudiced toward new neighbors.

forelsket.explanation: "Forelsket" means "in love", often the early, exciting stage: Jeg er forelsket i dig (I am in love with you). Use i (in) to say who the person is. At blive forelsket (to fall in love) is the moment it starts.

sentence.da: De er **forelsket** og smiler hele tiden.
sentence.en: They are in love and smile all the time.

foreløbig.explanation: "Foreløbig" means "for the time being", so that something holds for now but may change later. It also means "preliminary", describing a first version that is not yet settled.

forms.en: For now we know no more

sentence.da: Vi har **foreløbig** ingen svar fra kommunen.
sentence.en: For the time being, we have no answer from the municipality.

foreningsliv.explanation: "Foreningsliv" means "club and association life", the whole world of sports clubs, choirs and groups that people join in their free time. It is built from en forening (an association) and et liv (a life).

sentence.da: I byens **foreningsliv** kan både børn og voksne spille og synge sammen.
sentence.en: In the town's club life, both children and adults can play and sing together.

forestående.explanation: "Forestående" means "upcoming" or "impending", about something that will happen soon, often something serious: en forestående krise (an impending crisis).

sentence.da: Hele byen forbereder sig på den **forestående** storm.
sentence.en: The whole town is preparing for the impending storm.

forfra.explanation: "Forfra" means "from the beginning" and also "from the front": Kan vi tage det forfra? (Can we do it from the beginning?) Han kom bagfra (He came from behind) is the opposite of coming from the front.

sentence.da: Jeg tog fejl, og nu må jeg begynde **forfra**.
sentence.en: I made a mistake, and now I must begin again.

forfærdelig.explanation: "Forfærdelig" means "terrible" and is stronger than dårlig (bad): Det var en forfærdelig ulykke (It was a terrible accident).

sentence.da: Det var en **forfærdelig** ulykke på motorvejen.
sentence.en: It was a terrible accident on the highway.

forgiftet.explanation: "Forgiftet" means "poisoned", harmed by something toxic, for a person, an animal, or even water or food. It is also used for a bad mood: en forgiftet stemning (a poisoned atmosphere).

sentence.da: Fiskene døde, fordi vandet i søen var **forgiftet**.
sentence.en: The fish died because the water in the lake was poisoned.

forgængelig.explanation: "Forgængelig" means "transient", bound to pass away sooner or later. It is used for big things such as life and fame. For food that spoils, Danes usually say letfordærvelig (perishable).

sentence.da: Skønhed er **forgængelig**, men gode minder varer ved.
sentence.en: Beauty is transient, but good memories last.

forgæves.explanation: "Forgæves" means "in vain": you made an effort, but it did not give the result you wanted. It usually comes right after the verb.

sentence.da: Han prøvede **forgæves** at åbne den låste dør.
sentence.en: He tried in vain to open the locked door.

forhastet.explanation: "Forhastet" means "hasty", done too quickly without enough thought. It is used about decisions, conclusions and actions rather than about speed itself: hurtig (fast) is the word for a quick walker.

sentence.da: Han tog en **forhastet** beslutning og fortrød den bagefter.
sentence.en: He made a hasty decision and regretted it afterwards.

forholdsvis.explanation: "Forholdsvis" means "relatively" and softens a description: something is so only when you compare it with what is normal. It goes right before the word it describes.

sentence.da: Huset er gammelt, men taget er **forholdsvis** nyt.
sentence.en: The house is old, but the roof is relatively new.

forhåbentlig.explanation: "Forhåbentlig" means "hopefully" and shows something you wish for: Forhåbentlig bliver det godt vejr (Hopefully the weather will be good). It says the same as Jeg håber, at det bliver godt vejr (I hope the weather will be good).

sentence.da: **Forhåbentlig** kommer toget til tiden i dag.
sentence.en: Hopefully the train comes on time today.

forinden.explanation: "Forinden" means "beforehand" and points to the time before an event you have just named, or that everyone knows about.

sentence.da: Mødet starter klokken ti, så læs mailen **forinden**.
sentence.en: The meeting starts at ten, so read the email beforehand.

forkert.explanation: "Forkert" means "wrong" or "incorrect", for answers, directions, numbers or choices.

sentence.da: Fem plus fem er tolv. Det er **forkert**.
sentence.en: Five plus five is twelve. That is wrong.

forkælet.explanation: "Forkælet" means "spoiled" about a person who gets too much and expects to always have their own way. Food that has gone bad is not forkælet but fordærvet (rotten).

sentence.da: Barnet er **forkælet**, fordi det altid får sin vilje.
sentence.en: The child is spoiled because it always gets its way.

forkølet.explanation: "Forkølet" means "having a cold". Jeg er forkølet means "I have a cold". It is milder than syg (sick).

sentence.da: Jeg er **forkølet** og hoster meget.
sentence.en: I have a cold and cough a lot.

forladt.explanation: "Forladt" means "abandoned": et forladt hus (an abandoned house). It also fits a person left alone: Han følte sig forladt (He felt abandoned).

sentence.da: Der står et **forladt** hus i skoven.
sentence.en: There is an abandoned house in the forest.

forlovet.explanation: "Forlovet" means "engaged" to marry: Jeg er forlovet med Anna (I am engaged to Anna). Use med (to) to say who the other person is.

sentence.da: Vi er **forlovet** og skal giftes næste år.
sentence.en: We are engaged and will get married next year.

formel.explanation: "Formel" means "formal", done in a correct way that follows set rules and proper manners. The same spelling is also en formel (a formula, as in math), so the rest of the sentence shows which one is meant.

sentence.da: Kontrakten er en **formel** aftale, og begge parter skriver under.
sentence.en: The contract is a formal agreement, and both parties sign.

formentlig.explanation: "Formentlig" means "presumably": you believe something is true, but you have not checked it and are not sure.

sentence.da: Jeg har ikke tjekket, men han er **formentlig** hjemme.
sentence.en: I have not checked, but he is presumably home.

fornuft.explanation: "Fornuft" means "reason" or "common sense", the ability to judge things well. It has no plural, just like the English words reason and common sense.

sentence.da: Hun har meget **fornuft** og tager aldrig overilede beslutninger.
sentence.en: She has a lot of common sense and never makes rash decisions.

fornuftig.explanation: "Fornuftig" means "sensible" and describes a choice or person that uses good sense: Det er fornuftigt at spare penge (It is sensible to save money). The opposite is dum (stupid).

sentence.da: Det er en **fornuftig** idé at tage en jakke med.
sentence.en: It is a sensible idea to bring a jacket.

fornærmet.explanation: "Fornærmet" means "offended" and describes a person who feels that someone has treated them with disrespect. It is about the person who feels it, not about the one who causes it.

sentence.da: Han blev **fornærmet**, da hun grinede af hans idé.
sentence.en: He was offended when she laughed at his idea.

forrest.explanation: "Forrest" means "at the front" and picks out the spot furthest ahead in a row, line or group.

forms.en: at the front of the line
at the front of the classroom

sentence.da: Børnene sidder **forrest**, så de kan se tavlen.
sentence.en: The children sit at the front so they can see the board.

forresten.explanation: "Forresten" means "by the way" and adds a thought that has just come to you: Forresten, har du set Mia? (By the way, have you seen Mia?).

forms.en: By the way, where do you live?
I know that, by the way.

sentence.da: **Forresten**, jeg har købt billetter til lørdag.
sentence.en: By the way, I have bought tickets for Saturday.

forrige.explanation: "Forrige" means "previous" and points to the one just before this one: i forrige måned (last month). It never changes: den forrige bil (the previous car), det forrige hus (the previous house).

sentence.da: Vi mødtes i **forrige** uge.
sentence.en: We met last week.

forsigtig.explanation: "Forsigtig" means "cautious" and describes someone who takes care to avoid risk: Han kører forsigtigt (He drives carefully). Vær forsigtig! is a common warning (Be careful!).

sentence.da: Vær **forsigtig**, gulvet er glat!
sentence.en: Be careful, the floor is slippery!

forsikring.explanation: "En forsikring" means "insurance", an agreement where you pay money regularly and the company pays for certain damage. To buy one, say at tegne en forsikring (to take out insurance).

sentence.da: Min **forsikring** dækker ikke vandskade.
sentence.en: My insurance does not cover water damage.

forsinket.explanation: "Forsinket" means "delayed" or "late", mostly for trains, buses and planes. About yourself you can also say Jeg er forsinket (I am late).

sentence.da: Toget er **forsinket** med tyve minutter.
sentence.en: The train is delayed by twenty minutes.

forskellig.explanation: "Forskellig" means "different", for things that are not alike: De to brødre er meget forskellige (The two brothers are very different). It also means "various": forskellige farver (various colors).

sentence.da: Vi har **forskellig** smag, men vi er gode venner.
sentence.en: We have different tastes, but we are good friends.

forskning.explanation: "Forskning" means "research", the careful work at universities and hospitals that finds new knowledge. Like the English word, it has no plural.

sentence.da: Staten giver penge til **forskning** i kræft og hjertesygdomme.
sentence.en: The state gives money to research on cancer and heart disease.

forskrækket.explanation: "Forskrækket" means "startled", suddenly frightened for a moment, for example by a loud bang or someone appearing behind you. The fear passes quickly.

sentence.da: Hunden blev **forskrækket** over den høje lyd.
sentence.en: The dog was startled by the loud noise.

forstoppet.explanation: "Forstoppet" means "constipated", having trouble emptying the bowels. It comes from stoppe (to stop up), so the idea is that something is blocked.

sentence.da: Hvis man er **forstoppet**, hjælper det at spise mere frugt.
sentence.en: If you are constipated, it helps to eat more fruit.

forståelig.explanation: "Forståelig" means "understandable" in two ways: easy enough to follow, or natural to feel. En forståelig reaktion (an understandable reaction) is one that makes sense given the situation.

sentence.da: Hans forklaring var kort og **forståelig**, så alle fulgte med.
sentence.en: His explanation was short and understandable, so everyone followed.

forståelsesfuld.explanation: "Forståelsesfuld" means "understanding" and describes a person who listens and accepts that others can have good reasons for how they feel. It is built from forståelse (understanding) and fuld (full), so it is literally "full of understanding".

sentence.da: Min chef er **forståelsesfuld**, når børnene er syge.
sentence.en: My boss is understanding when the children are sick.

forstående.explanation: "Forstående" means "understanding" and describes a person or a reaction that shows sympathy for someone else's situation. It is built from the verb at forstå (to understand) plus -ende, which works like the English -ing.

sentence.da: Hun gav mig et **forstående** nik, da jeg forklarede det.
sentence.en: She gave me an understanding nod when I explained it.

forstærkning.explanation: "En forstærkning" means "a reinforcement", something added to make a thing stronger or bigger. It is used for extra people sent to help, such as soldiers or police, and for making a sound louder.

sentence.da: Politiet bad om **forstærkning**, da folkemængden voksede.
sentence.en: The police asked for reinforcement when the crowd grew.

forsømt.explanation: "Forsømt" means "neglected", not given the care or attention it needed. It is used for places and things left to fall apart, and also for people, such as children. It comes from at forsømme (to fail to look after).

sentence.da: Huset var **forsømt**, og taget var begyndt at lække.
sentence.en: The house was neglected, and the roof had started to leak.

fortabt.explanation: "Fortabt" means "lost" in a serious sense: gone for good or beyond help, not just misplaced. To say you do not know the way, use at fare vild (to get lost) instead.

sentence.da: Uden håb og venner følte han sig **fortabt**.
sentence.en: Without hope and friends, he felt lost.

fortjent.explanation: "Fortjent" means "deserved" or "well earned", for something good you got because you worked for it.

sentence.da: Efter en lang uge er weekenden **fortjent**.
sentence.en: After a long week, the weekend is well deserved.

fortrinsvis.explanation: "Fortrinsvis" means "chiefly" or "mainly" and says that something is true in most cases, with a few exceptions. It goes right before the thing it points to.

sentence.da: Butikken sælger **fortrinsvis** dansk mad, men også lidt udenlandsk.
sentence.en: The shop mainly sells Danish food, but also a little foreign food.

fortrolig.explanation: "Fortrolig" means "confidential", something private that you should not pass on. It also means "familiar", when you know a person or a thing well enough to feel at ease: at være fortrolig med noget (to be familiar with something).

sentence.da: Jeg er ikke **fortrolig** med det nye system.
sentence.en: I am not familiar with the new system.

fortrolighed.explanation: "En fortrolighed" means "confidentiality", the duty to keep information to yourself, and also "familiarity", the ease between people who know each other well. It comes from fortrolig (confidential, familiar).

sentence.da: Alt, hvad du siger til lægen, bliver behandlet i **fortrolighed**.
sentence.en: Everything you tell the doctor is treated in confidence.

fortroligt.explanation: "Fortroligt" means "confidentially" or "in confidence", for things you tell one person who must keep them private: Jeg fortæller dig det fortroligt (I am telling you this in confidence). It also means "confidential": Dokumentet er fortroligt (The document is confidential).

forms.en: I am telling you this in confidence

sentence.da: Det er **fortroligt**. Sig det ikke til andre.
sentence.en: It is confidential. Do not tell anyone else.

fortsat.explanation: "Fortsat" means "still" or "continued": a situation goes on with no break. It is also what at fortsætte (to continue) turns into after jeg har: Jeg har fortsat med at læse (I have kept on reading).

forms.en: Have a good rest of your day!

sentence.da: Selv efter tre timer regner det **fortsat**.
sentence.en: Even after three hours it is still raining.

fortvivlet.explanation: "Fortvivlet" means "distraught" or "in despair" and describes a deep, helpless sadness when you do not know what to do. It is much stronger than ked af det (sad).

sentence.da: Hun var **fortvivlet**, fordi hun ikke kunne finde sit barn.
sentence.en: She was distraught because she could not find her child.

forud.explanation: "Forud" means "ahead" or "in advance", looking forward in place or time. It is mostly found in set expressions, and forud for followed by an event means before it: forud for valget (before the election).

sentence.da: Vi læser alle papirerne **forud** for mødet.
sentence.en: We read all the papers before the meeting.

forude.explanation: "Forude" means "ahead" and tells where something is: further along the way you are going. Like ude (outside) and inde (inside), the final -e shows where something is, not where it moves to.

sentence.da: Der er kø **forude**, så vi kommer for sent.
sentence.en: There is a traffic jam ahead, so we will be late.

foruden.explanation: "Foruden" means "besides" or "apart from" and adds something extra to what you have just named. It adds to the list; it does not leave anything out.

sentence.da: Til festen kom der **foruden** mig tre venner.
sentence.en: Besides me, three friends came to the party.

forudsat at.explanation: "Forudsat at" means "provided that" and names the one condition that must hold for the rest to be true. A small word like ikke goes before the verb after it: forudsat at han ikke kommer (provided that he does not come).

forms.en: provided that the weather is nice

sentence.da: Vi tager til stranden, **forudsat at** det ikke regner.
sentence.en: We are going to the beach, provided that it does not rain.

forurening.explanation: "En forurening" means "pollution", harmful substances that make air, water or soil dirty. It is often combined with the place, as in luftforurening (air pollution).

sentence.da: I byen gør **forurening** fra biler luften dårlig.
sentence.en: In the city, pollution from cars makes the air bad.

foruroligende.explanation: "Foruroligende" means "disturbing" or "alarming" and describes things that make you feel something may be wrong, such as news, signs and numbers.

sentence.da: Det er **foruroligende**, at så mange børn ikke kan svømme.
sentence.en: It is disturbing that so many children cannot swim.

forventningsfuld.explanation: "Forventningsfuld" means "expectant", looking forward to something good that is about to happen. It is made of forventning (an expectation) and -fuld (full of).

sentence.da: Pigen var meget **forventningsfuld** op til sin fødselsdag.
sentence.en: The girl was very expectant before her birthday.

forvirrende.explanation: "Forvirrende" means "confusing" and describes the thing that causes the mix-up in your head. The person who feels it is forvirret (confused).

sentence.da: Skiltene i byen er så **forvirrende**, at vi kører forkert.
sentence.en: The signs in the town are so confusing that we drive the wrong way.

forvirret.explanation: "Forvirret" means "confused", for when you do not understand what is going on.

sentence.da: Jeg er **forvirret**, fordi jeg ikke forstår det.
sentence.en: I am confused because I do not understand it.

forvirring.explanation: "Forvirring" means "confusion", when people do not understand what is going on. Someone who feels it is forvirret (confused): Jeg er helt forvirret (I am totally confused).

sentence.da: Der var **forvirring**, fordi alle talte på samme tid.
sentence.en: There was confusion because everyone talked at the same time.

forældet.explanation: "Forældet" means "outdated" and describes something too old to be useful or correct any more, such as a program, a law or a piece of information.

sentence.da: Programmet er **forældet**, så det virker ikke på nye telefoner.
sentence.en: The program is outdated, so it does not work on new phones.

forældre.explanation: "Forældre" means "parents", mother and father together. For just one parent, say en forælder (a parent).

sentence.da: Min mor og min far er mine **forældre**.
sentence.en: My mom and my dad are my parents.

forældreløs.explanation: "Forældreløs" means "orphaned", without parents. It is built from forældre (parents) and løs (without), the same ending as in hjemløs (homeless) and søvnløs (sleepless).

sentence.da: Efter ulykken blev drengen **forældreløs** og kom til en plejefamilie.
sentence.en: After the accident the boy became an orphan and went to a foster family.

forældremyndighed.explanation: "En forældremyndighed" means "custody", the legal right and duty to make decisions for a child, such as where the child lives and goes to school. When it is shared, it is called fælles forældremyndighed (joint custody).

sentence.da: Efter skilsmissen fik moren **forældremyndighed** over børnene.
sentence.en: After the divorce, the mother got custody of the children.

fra.explanation: "Fra" means "from" and works for places, people and times. Its opposite is til (to): en gave til mig (a gift for me) versus en gave fra mig (a gift from me).

sentence.da: Toget kører **fra** København til Aarhus.
sentence.en: The train goes from Copenhagen to Aarhus.

fra nu af.explanation: "Fra nu af" means "from now on" and looks forward, often for a new rule or decision. To look back instead, use indtil nu (until now).

forms.da: Fra nu af spiser jeg sundt.
forms.en: From now on I eat healthy.

forms.da: Fra nu af kommer jeg tidligt.
forms.en: From now on I come early.

forms.da: Fra nu af er det mit job.
forms.en: From now on it is my job.

sentence.da: Jeg går i seng klokken ti **fra nu af**.
sentence.en: I go to bed at ten from now on.

fra tid til anden.explanation: "Fra tid til anden" means "from time to time", for things that happen occasionally with no fixed pattern. If the phrase starts the sentence, the verb comes right after it: Fra tid til anden kommer han forbi (From time to time he comes by).

forms.da: Vi ses fra tid til anden
forms.en: We see each other from time to time

forms.da: Jeg ringer fra tid til anden
forms.en: I call from time to time

forms.da: Hun besøger os fra tid til anden
forms.en: She visits us from time to time

sentence.da: Vi spiser ude **fra tid til anden**, men ikke hver uge.
sentence.en: We eat out from time to time, but not every week.

fragt.explanation: "En fragt" means "shipping" or "freight": the cost of sending goods, or the goods being carried, as in et fragtskib (a cargo ship).

sentence.da: Webshoppen tager 50 kroner i **fragt**.
sentence.en: The web shop charges 50 kroner for shipping.

frankrig.explanation: "Frankrig" means "France", a large country in western Europe. It is written with a capital letter.

sentence.da: Paris ligger i **Frankrig**.
sentence.en: Paris is in France.

fransk.explanation: "Fransk" means "French", for things from France and for the language. It is written with a small letter: Jeg taler fransk (I speak French).

sentence.da: Hun kommer fra Frankrig og taler **fransk**.
sentence.en: She comes from France and speaks French.

franskbrød.explanation: "Et franskbrød" means "a white loaf", the ordinary light kind. It is made of fransk (French) and brød (bread). Rugbrød (rye bread) is the dark, heavy kind.

sentence.da: **Franskbrød** er lyst og blødt brød.
sentence.en: White bread is light, soft bread.

fraskilt.explanation: "Fraskilt" means "divorced" and says what someone is now: Min onkel er fraskilt (My uncle is divorced). To talk about the event, say at blive skilt: De blev skilt i fjor (They got divorced last year).

sentence.da: Mine forældre er **fraskilt** og bor hver for sig.
sentence.en: My parents are divorced and live separately.

fravær.explanation: "Et fravær" means "absence": not being where you are expected, especially at school or work. In both places it is also the count of days you have missed.

sentence.da: Eleven har meget **fravær**, fordi hun ofte er syg.
sentence.en: The student has a lot of absence because she is often ill.

fraværende.explanation: "Fraværende" means "absent" and "absent-minded". It can say that someone is not there, or that they are there but their mind is elsewhere: Han virker fraværende i dag (He seems out of it today).

sentence.da: Han sidder ved bordet, men er helt **fraværende**.
sentence.en: He sits at the table, but is completely absent-minded.

fred.explanation: "Fred" means "peace", the opposite of war and also a quiet, undisturbed time: Folk ønsker fred (People want peace). Lad mig være i fred (Leave me alone, literally "let me be in peace").

sentence.da: Landet har haft **fred** i mange år.
sentence.en: The country has had peace for many years.

fredag.explanation: "Fredag" means "Friday". På fredag means "on Friday" (the coming one) and om fredagen means "on Fridays" (every Friday). Day names are written with a small letter.

sentence.da: Efter torsdag kommer **fredag**.
sentence.en: After Thursday comes Friday.

fredelig.explanation: "Fredelig" means "peaceful" and describes calm places, people and times. It is built from fred (peace) and also fits a protest without fighting: en fredelig demonstration (a peaceful protest).

sentence.da: Landsbyen er stille og **fredelig**.
sentence.en: The village is quiet and peaceful.

frelse.explanation: "En frelse" means "salvation", in religion being delivered from sin and death. In everyday speech, it is a great help that arrives just in time: Din hjælp var en frelse (Your help was a godsend).

sentence.da: I kristendommen handler **frelse** om tilgivelse for synd.
sentence.en: In Christianity, salvation is about forgiveness of sin.

fremfor.explanation: "Fremfor" means "rather than" and "over", placing one choice above another: Jeg vælger tog fremfor bil (I choose the train over the car).

sentence.da: Mange danskere cykler **fremfor** at køre bil.
sentence.en: Many Danes bike rather than drive a car.

fremgang.explanation: "En fremgang" means "progress", getting better over time at school, in sport or in health. It is built from frem (forward) and gang (going), so it is literally "going forward".

sentence.da: Efter tre måneders træning kan jeg se **fremgang**.
sentence.en: After three months of training I can see progress.

fremmed.explanation: "Fremmed" means "foreign" or "strange": et fremmed sprog (a foreign language). On its own, en fremmed means "a stranger": Jeg talte med en fremmed (I talked to a stranger).

sentence.da: Det er et **fremmed** sprog for mig.
sentence.en: It is a foreign language to me.

fremover.explanation: "Fremover" means "from now on", a change that starts today and lasts. It is used to set a new habit or rule. At the start of a sentence, the verb comes right after it.

forms.en: From now on I take the bike
We will see each other more often from now on
From now on you must call first

sentence.da: Jeg vil **fremover** gå i seng klokken ti.
sentence.en: From now on I will go to bed at ten.

fremragende.explanation: "Fremragende" means "excellent", clearly above average, and is often used for results, work and skills.

sentence.da: Hans karakterer er **fremragende**, fordi han læser hver dag.
sentence.en: His grades are excellent because he studies every day.

fremtidig.explanation: "Fremtidig" means "future" and describes a person or thing that will be something later. The thing itself is fremtiden (the future): Vi tænker på fremtiden (We think about the future).

sentence.da: Hun er en **fremtidig** kollega.
sentence.en: She is a future colleague.

fremtrædende.explanation: "Fremtrædende" means "prominent", standing out because of importance or position. It is made of frem (forward) and at træde (to step), so a prominent person steps forward from the crowd.

sentence.da: Hun er en **fremtrædende** forsker inden for medicin.
sentence.en: She is a prominent researcher in medicine.

fri.explanation: "Fri" means "free" and also "off" from work or school: Jeg har fri means "I am off work". It does not mean free of charge; for that use gratis.

sentence.da: I dag har jeg **fri** fra arbejde.
sentence.en: Today I am off work.

frisk.explanation: "Frisk" means "fresh", for food and air. For a person it means "healthy": Jeg er frisk means "I am well".

sentence.da: Jeg købte mælken i dag. Den er **frisk**.
sentence.en: I bought the milk today. It is fresh.

fritid.explanation: "Fritid" means "free time", the time when you are not at work or school.

sentence.da: I min **fritid** går jeg ture.
sentence.en: In my free time I go for walks.

frivillig.explanation: "Frivillig" means "voluntary", done because you choose to, not because you must. As a person, en frivillig is "a volunteer": Vi har brug for frivillige (We need volunteers).

sentence.da: Deltagelsen er **frivillig**, og man kan sige nej.
sentence.en: Taking part is voluntary, and you can say no.

frodig.explanation: "Frodig" means "lush", growing thickly and healthily. It is used mostly for plants, grass and landscapes that are thick and green.

sentence.da: Efter al regnen er haven blevet **frodig** og grøn.
sentence.en: After all the rain, the garden has become lush and green.

sentence.da: Klokken er tolv. Vi spiser **frokost**.
sentence.en: It is twelve o'clock. We eat lunch.

frossen.explanation: "Frossen" means "frozen", food that has been kept so cold that it is hard. For a person who feels cold, do not use it: Danes say jeg fryser (I am cold, literally I freeze).

sentence.da: Pizzaen i fryseren er **frossen**.
sentence.en: The pizza in the freezer is frozen.

frost.explanation: "Frost" means "frost", the cold when it is below freezing outside: Der er frost i nat (There is frost tonight). It also means the white ice on a window: Der er frost på ruden (There is frost on the window).

sentence.da: Når der er **frost**, fryser vandet til is.
sentence.en: When there is frost, the water freezes to ice.

frostklar.explanation: "Frostklar" means "crisp and frosty", describing a day or night with frost and a clear sky. It is made of frost (frost) and klar (clear), and is used mostly about winter.

sentence.da: Det var en **frostklar** nat med tusindvis af stjerner.
sentence.en: It was a crisp, frosty night with thousands of stars.

frostvarer.explanation: "Frostvarer" means "frozen foods", products that are sold and stored frozen. It is made of frost (frost) and varer (goods) and is used mostly in the plural.

sentence.da: I butikken holder **frostvarer** som ærter og fisk sig længe.
sentence.en: In the shop, frozen foods like peas and fish keep for a long time.

frustreret.explanation: "Frustreret" means "frustrated", the feeling when things do not work out: Jeg er frustreret over computeren (I am frustrated with the computer). Det er frustrerende (It is frustrating) describes the thing itself.

sentence.da: Han er **frustreret**, fordi printeren ikke virker.
sentence.en: He is frustrated because the printer does not work.

frygt.explanation: "Frygt" means "fear": Hun følte frygt (She felt fear). To say you are afraid, use bange: Jeg er bange (I am afraid).

sentence.da: Hun kunne ikke skjule sin **frygt**.
sentence.en: She could not hide her fear.

frygtelig.explanation: "Frygtelig" means "terrible", for something awful or scary.

sentence.da: Stormen var **frygtelig**, og træer faldt om.
sentence.en: The storm was terrible, and trees fell over.

frygtløs.explanation: "Frygtløs" means "fearless", without fear. It is built from frygt (fear) and løs (without). A modig (brave) person may feel fear and act anyway, but a frygtløs person feels none.

sentence.da: Hun er **frygtløs** og springer fra tre meters højde.
sentence.en: She is fearless and jumps from a height of three meters.

fræk.explanation: "Fræk" means "cheeky" or "naughty", often for a child who tests the limits: Hvor er du fræk! (How cheeky you are!). It also fits a daring joke: en fræk vittighed (a naughty joke).

sentence.da: Den lille dreng var meget **fræk** i dag.
sentence.en: The little boy was very naughty today.

fugtig.explanation: "Fugtig" means "damp" or "humid", for towels, walls and air: Håndklædet er fugtigt (The towel is damp). It is not the same as våd (wet), which means soaked.

sentence.da: Luften i badeværelset er meget **fugtig**.
sentence.en: The air in the bathroom is very humid.

fugtighed.explanation: "En fugtighed" means "humidity", the amount of water in the air or in a surface. The weather report gives it as a percentage.

sentence.da: Der er høj **fugtighed** i badeværelset efter et varmt bad.
sentence.en: There is high humidity in the bathroom after a hot bath.

fugtigt.explanation: "Fugtigt" means "humid" for air and "damp" for things: Håndklædet er stadig fugtigt (The towel is still damp). It is only a little wet, not the same as vådt (wet).

sentence.da: Der er **fugtigt** i kælderen.
sentence.en: It is damp in the basement.

fuld.explanation: "Fuld" means "full", for a glass, a bus or a room. When it describes a person, it means "drunk": Han er fuld means "He is drunk". To say you are full after a meal, use mæt (full after eating).

sentence.da: Bussen er helt **fuld** af mennesker.
sentence.en: The bus is completely full of people.

fuldført.explanation: "Fuldført" means "completed" and describes a task done all the way to the end, not just started. It is also what at fuldføre (to complete) turns into after jeg har: Jeg har fuldført kurset (I have completed the course).

sentence.da: Opgaven er **fuldført**, når alle punkter er markeret.
sentence.en: The task is completed when all items are marked.

fuldkommen.explanation: "Fuldkommen" means "perfect", without any flaw, and also "complete" or "total", used before a state or feeling: fuldkommen tavshed (complete silence).

sentence.da: Hun følte en **fuldkommen** ro, da hun så havet.
sentence.en: She felt a perfect calm when she saw the sea.

fuldkorn.explanation: "Fuldkorn" means "whole grain", the whole seed of the grain, used in bread and pasta: Jeg vælger fuldkorn (I choose whole grain). Added to another word, it describes it: fuldkornspasta (whole-grain pasta).

sentence.da: **Fuldkorn** er sundt, fordi det har mange fibre.
sentence.en: Whole grain is healthy because it has a lot of fiber.

fuldstændig.explanation: "Fuldstændig" means "completely" and makes a word as strong as it can be: Hun har fuldstændig ret (She is completely right). It also describes things that miss nothing: et fuldstændigt svar (a complete answer).

sentence.da: Jeg har **fuldstændig** glemt hans navn.
sentence.en: I have completely forgotten his name.

fuldt booket.explanation: "Fuldt booket" means "fully booked", with nothing free left. For tickets to a show, say udsolgt (sold out).

forms.da: Vi er fuldt booket i juli
forms.en: We are fully booked in July

sentence.da: Desværre er hotellet **fuldt booket** i weekenden.
sentence.en: Unfortunately, the hotel is fully booked this weekend.

fyldestgørende.explanation: "Fyldestgørende" means "satisfactory", complete enough to cover everything that was asked or needed. It is used for answers, explanations and information.

sentence.da: Lærerens forklaring var kort, men **fyldestgørende**.
sentence.en: The teacher's explanation was short but satisfactory.

fyldig.explanation: "Fyldig" means "full" or "rich", describing food, drink or a sound with a lot of body and depth. It is typical for red wine and soup, and also a deep voice: en fyldig stemme (a full voice).

sentence.da: Vinen er **fyldig**, med smag af mørke bær.
sentence.en: The wine is full-bodied, with a taste of dark berries.

fyldt.explanation: "Fyldt" means "full" or "filled", for something that has been filled up. For a person who has eaten enough, use mæt (full).

sentence.da: Hans lommer er **fyldt** med slik.
sentence.en: His pockets are filled with candy.

fyrre.explanation: "Fyrre" means "forty". Do not mix it up with fire (four): fire kroner is four kroner, fyrre kroner is forty kroner. For 41, you say enogfyrre, literally one-and-forty.

sentence.da: Jeg er **fyrre** år gammel.
sentence.en: I am forty years old.

fyrværkeri.explanation: "Fyrværkeri" means "fireworks" and is used for the whole display. For one single rocket, say en raket (a rocket).

sentence.da: **Fyrværkeri** lyser op på nattehimlen.
sentence.en: Fireworks light up the night sky.

fysik.explanation: "Fysik" means "physics", the study of forces, light and energy. For a school class, you leave out en: Jeg har fysik efter frokost (I have physics after lunch).

sentence.da: I **fysik** lærer vi om lys og lyd.
sentence.en: In physics we learn about light and sound.

fysisk.explanation: "Fysisk" means "physical", about the body or about real things you can touch: fysisk arbejde (physical work). Et fysisk møde (an in-person meeting) happens in real life, not online.

sentence.da: Løb og svømning er god **fysisk** træning.
sentence.en: Running and swimming are good physical exercise.

fælles.explanation: "Fælles" means "shared" or "common", for what belongs to several people together: Vi har et fælles køkken (We have a shared kitchen). It also fits a person two people both know.

sentence.da: Vi har en **fælles** ven i Aarhus.
sentence.en: We have a mutual friend in Aarhus.

fælleskøn.explanation: "Et fælleskøn" means "common gender", the group of Danish words that go with en: en dag (a day), en stol (a chair). In everyday talk people simply say en-ord (en-word).

sentence.da: Ordet bil hører til **fælleskøn**, så det hedder en bil.
sentence.en: The word car belongs to common gender, so it is en bil.

fængslende.explanation: "Fængslende" means "captivating" and describes something that holds your attention completely, such as a story, a speech or a film. It comes from at fængsle (to imprison), so it literally grabs and holds you.

sentence.da: Bogen er så **fængslende**, at jeg læser hele natten.
sentence.en: The book is so captivating that I read all night.

færdig.explanation: "Færdig" means "finished" or "done", for example after a meal or at the end of work. Do not mix it up with klar (ready), which means prepared to start: Er du klar? (Are you ready?).

sentence.da: Jeg har skrevet brevet. Nu er jeg **færdig**.
sentence.en: I have written the letter. Now I am done.

færdig med.explanation: "Færdig med" means "finished with". After med (with) you put the thing (færdig med lektierne, finished with the homework) or an action starting with at (færdig med at spise, finished eating).

forms.en: Are you finished with the book?

forms.da: Vi er færdige med at spise.

sentence.da: Nu er jeg **færdig med** arbejdet.
sentence.en: Now I am finished with work.

færdiglavet.explanation: "Færdiglavet" means "ready-made", mostly for food that is already cooked, so you only have to heat it up. It is built from færdig (ready) and lavet (made).

sentence.da: Supermarkedet sælger **færdiglavet** mad til dem, der har travlt.
sentence.en: The supermarket sells ready-made food for people who are busy.

færre.explanation: "Færre" means "fewer" and goes with things you can count: færre biler (fewer cars). For something you cannot count, use mindre (less): mindre støj (less noise).

sentence.da: Der er **færre** stole end gæster.
sentence.en: There are fewer chairs than guests.

færøerne.explanation: "Færøerne" means "the Faroe Islands", a group of islands in the North Atlantic that belong to the Kingdom of Denmark but govern themselves in many matters. It is always plural, and Danes say på Færøerne (on the Faroe Islands), like for other islands.

sentence.da: **Færøerne** ligger i Atlanterhavet mellem Skotland og Island.
sentence.en: The Faroe Islands lie in the Atlantic between Scotland and Iceland.

færøsk.explanation: "Færøsk" means "Faroese", both for things from the Faroe Islands and for the language spoken there. Like other languages and nationalities in Danish, it is written with a small letter.

sentence.da: Hun er fra Tórshavn og taler **færøsk** derhjemme.
sentence.en: She is from Tórshavn and speaks Faroese at home.

føj.explanation: "Føj" means "yuck" and shows disgust at a smell, a taste or something dirty: Føj, det lugter forfærdeligt! (Yuck, that smells awful!). Parents also say it to children: Føj, læg den fra dig (Yuck, put it down).

sentence.da: **Føj**, der er en edderkop i badekarret!
sentence.en: Yuck, there is a spider in the bathtub!

følelsesmæssigt.explanation: "Følelsesmæssigt" means "emotionally" and puts the focus on feelings. The ending -mæssigt means "in terms of", so tidsmæssigt means "time-wise".

sentence.da: Han er stærk fysisk, men **følelsesmæssigt** er han sårbar.
sentence.en: He is strong physically, but emotionally he is vulnerable.

følgende.explanation: "Følgende" means "following", the next thing in a list or in time: Læs følgende tekst (Read the following text). The word looks the same with en-words, et-words and plurals.

sentence.da: Den **følgende** dag skinnede solen igen.
sentence.en: The following day the sun shone again.

følsom.explanation: "Følsom" means "sensitive" and is used for people who feel things strongly, and for skin or things that react easily: Hun er følsom over for kritik (She is sensitive to criticism). Jeg har følsom hud (I have sensitive skin).

sentence.da: Han er **følsom** og græder let ved triste film.
sentence.en: He is sensitive and cries easily at sad movies.

før.explanation: "Før" means "before" in time. For place, use foran (in front of): foran huset (in front of the house).

sentence.da: Klokken fire er **før** klokken fem.
sentence.en: Four o'clock is before five o'clock.

førdatid.explanation: "En førdatid" means "past perfect", the tense built with havde or var plus a verb: Hun var gået, da jeg kom (She had left when I came).

sentence.da: Man bruger **førdatid** om noget, der skete før noget andet.
sentence.en: You use past perfect about something that happened before something else.

førende.explanation: "Førende" means "leading" and describes the best or most important one in a field, not the one who goes first in a line. It comes from at føre (to lead).

sentence.da: Han er den **førende** ekspert i dansk grammatik.
sentence.en: He is the leading expert in Danish grammar.

førnutid.explanation: "En førnutid" means "present perfect", the tense with har or er plus a verb, for what has happened up to now: Jeg har købt brød (I have bought bread).

sentence.da: Man bruger **førnutid**, når noget er sket og stadig betyder noget nu.
sentence.en: You use present perfect when something has happened and still matters now.

først.explanation: "Først" means "first" or "not until". Jeg kommer først i morgen means "I am not coming until tomorrow". Do not mix it up with første (the first one): den første dag (the first day).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **først** og går bagefter.
sentence.en: We eat first and go afterwards.

først og fremmest.explanation: "Først og fremmest" means "first and foremost". It introduces the most important point, so what comes after it matters most.

forms.da: Først og fremmest skal du hvile.
forms.en: First and foremost, you must rest.

sentence.da: **Først og fremmest** skal du hvile dig.
sentence.en: First and foremost, you need to rest.

første.explanation: "Første" means "first" in a list or order. It is used in dates: den første maj (the first of May), written 1. maj. Do not mix it up with først, which tells when something happens: Først spiser vi (First we eat).

sentence.da: Januar er årets **første** måned.
sentence.en: January is the first month of the year.

førstehjælp.explanation: "Førstehjælp" means "first aid", the help you give right away to someone who is hurt. It is built from første (first) and hjælp (help). The kit you keep at home is en førstehjælpskasse (a first aid box).

sentence.da: Man giver **førstehjælp**, når nogen kommer til skade.
sentence.en: You give first aid when someone gets hurt.
